question: Crow2020 has median 3.9 M read pairs (224 of 346 libraries below 5 M); Xue2021 is QuantSeq 3' tag-seq (79-86 nt). The strict MaizExpressN rule is >= 5 M mapped reads (>= 2 M for 3' tag-seq).
proposed_answer: Keep 5 M for standard RNA-seq and 2 M for 3' tag-seq (Xue2021). For Crow2020, decide: apply 5 M (drops most of it), lower to 2 M for this study, or keep only libraries above 5 M.
evidence: Crow2020 and Xue2021 review files; library_exclusions.py
decision: accepted, with a 2 M mapped-read floor for Crow2020 (Rubén, 20 Oct 2026)

question: Xue2021 (both GEO series) is QuantSeq 3' FWD single-end.
proposed_answer: Process like Huang2025 in MaizExpressN: no length correction (NO_LENGTH, TAG_STUDIES).
evidence: Xue2021 review file

question: Meng2025 stress libraries are cold (4 °C) plus high soil moisture with no cold-only arm; Zhang2017's greenhouse arm moves plants from greenhouse to a cold chamber with lower light.
proposed_answer: Keep both as their own contrasts (other_factor) and leave them out of cold-only pooled estimates (display only).
evidence: Meng2025 and Zhang2017 review files

question: Li2025, Yu2021, Wang2023, Zeng2021, Li2022c (mutant), He2016 and Liu2026 have a baseline (0 h or untimed) control rather than a control sampled at each time point.
proposed_answer: Use the baseline as control and tag the contrasts not_time_matched; keep them in pooling, as decided for MaizExpressN.
evidence: study review files

question: Bozic2025 (one library per condition), He2016 (no replication) and Zhou2022's TC time course (unreplicated).
proposed_answer: Display only; never pooled.
evidence: study review files

question: Crow2020 (cool vs warm chambers from sowing) and the low-temperature germination studies (Jiang2023, Li2022d, Zhang2020?, Zhang2024, Meng2022a) differ from acute chilling of seedlings.
proposed_answer: Separate contrast classes (chronic growth temperature; germination) at M4, not pooled with acute chilling.
evidence: phase = chronic in samples.tsv

question: Some controls are themselves cool: Zhang2024 15 °C, Frey2020 18 °C (vs 12 °C), Sommer2025 mild cold 16/12 °C as a treatment level.
proposed_answer: Keep; the contrast records both temperatures so users can filter.
evidence: Zhang2024, Frey2020, Sommer2025 review files

question: Friero2023 (PRJNA877073: submitter, funders and design match the authors) and Liao2026 (PRJDB41168: China Agricultural University, released before publication, design matches).
proposed_answer: Accept both as the studies' own data.
evidence: Friero2023 and Liao2026 review files

question: Zhou2024 (PAIRED libraries but one FASTQ per run), Zhao2021 (SINGLE ~299 nt, likely merged mates) and Friero2023 (one FASTQ for a PAIRED library).
proposed_answer: Inspect a FASTQ of each at M3 and quantify as single-end or split mates accordingly.
evidence: study review files

question: For root-only or shoot-only chilling, temperature_C holds the chilled site's temperature; the sampled organ's own temperature is in curation_note.
proposed_answer: Keep this encoding; contrasts at M4 will name local vs distal explicitly.
evidence: Xue2021 review file

question: Crow2020 B73-haplotype siblings are 'other inbred' (could count as B73 for B73-only pooling); Zhang2024 Zhengdan958 is a known hybrid but the paper doesn't say; Meng2025 set B genotype unrecorded (probably JD441).
proposed_answer: Keep as curated unless Rubén prefers B73 for the Crow2020 Low-haplotype siblings.
evidence: Crow2020, Zhang2024, Meng2025 review files

question: The paper calls CG60 'more cold tolerant' than CG102 (biomass ratio cold/control 0.54 vs 0.47, smaller Fv/Fm drop); the labels are relative, from two lines, not from field data.
proposed_answer: CG60 = tolerant, CG102 = sensitive (relative to each other).
evidence: Methods 'Plant growth conditions' (PMC6196024)

question: Controls for D1 and D4 are separate plantings (planted 1 and 3 d after the cold-treated plants, so 13 and 14 d old at sampling), and 'the experiment was repeated three times'. Is replicate R1-R3 a full independent repeat (all genotypes x treatments x days together)?
proposed_answer: Treat R1-R3 as independent repeats with matched controls; consider replicate as a blocking factor.
evidence: Methods (PMC6196024); BioSample attribute 'replicate'

question: time_h for recovery samples set to 96 h (72 h cold + 24 h recovery; 17 d after planting vs cold onset at 13 d). Controls get time_h 24 (D1) and 96 (D4) to be time-matched.
proposed_answer: Keep as entered.
evidence: Methods: cold started at V2, 13 d after planting; D1 = 14 d, D4 = 17 d after planting

question: Each genotype x treatment x time has a single library (8 libraries, one per condition).
proposed_answer: Keep all 8 (include = TRUE). DESeq2-based contrasts will be unreplicated (display only, no SE); the paper used edgeR for 'two samples per treatment' (one per line per time).
evidence: Paper Methods: 'There were eight samples in total: two samples per treatment condition (C, T), per time point (6h, 24h), and per inbred line' read as one library per line x condition x time; ENA lists 8 runs.

question: The paper does not say which plant part was harvested (30 seedlings per sample).
proposed_answer: Whole seedling (as a whole 5-day-old seedling) with po_term empty.
evidence: Paper Methods: 'Samples of 30 maize seedlings per inbred line were taken after 6 h and 24 h'; catalogue notes 'plant part not specified'.

question: BioSample names the lines LT (tolerant) and LS (susceptible); the paper's names are Zemun Polje lines whose assignment of Lancaster vs semi-dent heterotic groups to the lines was lost in the retrieved text.
proposed_answer: genotype LT / LS as in BioSample; other inbred; heterotic groups not recorded.
evidence: BioSample attribute genotype LT/LS, title 'Tolerant/Sensitive genotype, Control/Treatment, 6h/24h'.

question: Controls were kept at 25/20 C in the same chamber settings and sampled at the same time as treated seedlings; seedlings were germinated in the dark for 5 d.
proposed_answer: time_h = 6 or 24 for both control and treated samples. Day/night temperatures recorded in temperature_C / temperature_night_C.
evidence: Paper Methods: 'Control plants (C) were grown under optimal conditions (25/20 C - 12/12 h photoperiod ...) in the same period and sampled at identical time points'.

question: rRNA-depleted directional libraries (Ribo-Zero Plus), not poly(A) selected; PE150 NovaSeq 6000; 90-120 M read pairs per library.
proposed_answer: Note for pipeline QC: strandedness and non-polyA content differ from most other studies.
evidence: Paper Methods 2.2; ENA read_count 88-120 M.

question: Which of the 346 libraries come from the PT family and which from the Mi21 family, and from experimental replicate 1 (March 2017) or 2 (April 2017)?
proposed_answer: Not recoverable from the repository. Samples are pooled by tissue x temperature x Inv4m genotype (6-13 libraries per group) and replicate numbers follow alias order; donor and experimental replicate are not modelled. If a mapping is obtained (authors, or SNP-based donor assignment from the reads later), add it to other_factor/other_factor_level and use it as a blocking factor.
evidence: BioSample attributes hold only alias, tissue, dev_stage, temp, genotype and the library file name (GC72_P1_ILLSINHA14 style: lane GC72 = plates P1-P3, GC73 = plates P4-P6, barcode ILLSINHA1-96); no donor, family, plant or replicate field. ENA library_name = file name, experiment title only 'RNA seq of Zea mays: <tissue>'. No GEO series; PLOS supplement has no sample table (S1-S6 Fig, S1-S4 Table are figures and tables on emergence and candidate genes). Paper Methods: 2 donors (PT, Mi21) x 2 experimental replicates x 3 biological replicates per tissue x temperature x genotype. Alias increases with plate and barcode, so it is deposit order, not design order. Every plate holds both temperatures and both genotypes (about 2 B73 + 2 Inv4m per tissue x temperature x plate).

item: run count vs paper (346 vs 379 vs 432)
question: Why are only 346 libraries deposited when the paper analysed 379 (and planned 432)?
proposed_answer: Keep all 346 deposited libraries (include = TRUE). Missing 86 relative to the plan: 17 warm and 69 cold. Cool-chamber samples are the most depleted, so cool vs warm contrasts have fewer replicates than the design suggests (cells of 6-13 libraries per tissue x temperature x genotype, instead of 12).
evidence: Paper: 432 planned (9 tissues x 2 temperatures x 2 donors x 2 genotypes x 3 reps x 2 experimental replicates), 53 excluded for < 100,000 reads, 379 analysed. Data availability statement: 'All 346 files are available from the SRA'. BioProject PRJNA640392: 346 experiments, 346 BioSamples. Deposited: 199 warm, 147 cold; 190 B73-labelled, 156 Inv4m-labelled. Smallest deposited library is 283,250 read pairs, so the 53 low-read samples were evidently not deposited; the other 33 analysed samples are unexplained. Paper also says it sequenced 435 family samples (3 more than 432).

item: B73-labelled libraries: Low-haplotype siblings or B73 controls?
question: Does genotype 'B73' in the BioSample metadata mean the Inv4m-Low homozygous siblings from the PT and Mi21 BC5S1 families, or does it include the extra B73 control plants the authors sequenced in parallel?
proposed_answer: Treat all 190 B73-labelled libraries as Low-haplotype (B73 allele) homozygous siblings, as the paper's design implies, and keep them in one group. Ask the authors if B73 controls are mixed in.
evidence: Paper: RNA was also sequenced from 46 B73, 48 PT and 47 B73xPT F1 plants 'run in parallel with the families but not otherwise used in this experiment' (141 libraries besides the 435 family libraries). All 346 deposited libraries carry only the labels B73 or Inv4m. Four warm B73 cells hold 13 libraries (V3_Primary_root, V3_S2_leaf_base, V3_Stem_SAM, V3_leaf_sheath), one more than the design allows (12 per genotype x tissue x temperature), which may indicate a non-family B73 plant or one of the 3 extra family samples.

question: Which genotype_class should the two genotypes get? Both carry the B73 background; Inv4m is a mexicana-derived highland inversion introgressed by 5 backcrosses to B73 (about 3 % residual donor DNA elsewhere, mostly on chromosomes 2-5 depending on the family).
proposed_answer: Both classes 'other inbred' (introgression / near-isogenic lines, per spec), background B73, so the pair is a near-isogenic comparison. If B73-only pooled results should include the B73-haplotype siblings, change those 190 rows to 'B73'.
evidence: Paper: BC5S1 families segregating for the highland Inv4m haplotype, donors PT (Palomero Toluqueno, mexi5) and Mi21 (Conico, Michoacan 21); residual landrace alleles 7,236 genes (PT) and 4,095 genes (Mi21) across several blocks. Catalogue row flags the highland material as teosinte-derived introgression. Genotype strings used: 'B73-haplotype (Inv4m low) homozygous' and 'Inv4m (highland haplotype) homozygous'; the paper names them Low and High haplotype homozygous.

question: Which Table 1 tissue is the deposited label V3_Leaf_tissue?
proposed_answer: Probably 'V3 leaf tip, 5 cm of leaf tip', because it is the only V3 tissue of Table 1 without another deposited label. Recorded as 'V3 leaf tissue' in tissue_detail with that caveat; tissue_group Leaf is safe either way.
evidence: Table 1 lists V3 tissues Root, SAM, Sheath, Leaf base, Leaf tip, S2 leaf base, S2 leaf tip; deposited V3 labels are Primary_root, Stem_SAM, leaf_sheath, leaf_base, Leaf_tissue, S2_leaf_base, S2_leaf_tip. Table 2 row labels use 'V1 Leaf tissue' and 'V3 Leaf tissue'. Table 1 gives 'Pooled leaf tissue' for V1 leaf.

item: meaning of S2 and which leaf is sampled
question: What does 'S2' stand for, and which leaf (number) were leaf base, leaf tip and S2 leaf sampled from?
proposed_answer: Describe S2 as 'youngest sampled leaf' (the paper's own words) and leave leaf numbers unspecified.
evidence: The paper never defines 'S2'. Results: 'the youngest developmental leaf that we sampled' and 'basal (developmentally immature) section of the S2 leaf'. Table 1: 5 cm of leaf base and 5 cm of leaf tip for both the leaf and S2 leaf entries. S2 Fig (photographs of V3 shoot sampling, PDF) was not read.

question: Should chronic cool vs warm contrasts be read as stage-matched rather than age-matched?
proposed_answer: Yes. age_days left empty; contrasts compare plants at the same V stage (V1 or V3) grown cool vs warm. Cool plants are older at sampling.
evidence: Paper: tissues sampled when plants reached V1 (corner plants) or V3 (center plants), 2-4 h after simulated sunrise; emergence about 9 d in the cool and about 4 d in the warm chamber; sampling age not given. Chambers were swapped between the two experimental replicates (March and April 2017), so chamber and temperature are not fully confounded, but replicate labels are lost (see first item). Cool regime is 22/11 degC day/night, a chronic highland-like growth temperature, not a chilling treatment.

question: Will the library QC rules for this project exclude most Crow2020 libraries?
proposed_answer: Keep all as include = TRUE; let the depth and mapping rules decide at the library QC step.
evidence: ENA n_spots (read pairs): median 3.9 M, mean 4.4 M, minimum 0.28 M, maximum 21.6 M; 224 of 346 libraries below 5 M pairs and 72 below 2 M. Paper: mean 4.24 M reads per sample, random-primed strand-specific BRaD-seq, 96-plex per HiSeq X lane, 2 x 150 bp. A 5 M mapped-reads rule as in MaizExpressN would remove most of the study.

question: Is each library one tissue from one plant?
proposed_answer: pooled_plants left empty; assume one plant per library.
evidence: Paper: 432 samples from 96 plants (up to 9 tissues per plant); two seeds per pot, corner plant sampled at V1 and center plant at V3. Elsewhere the same paper says 81 plants were selected and 364 genotyped, which does not match the 96 plants.

question: Which cold-type contrasts does Crow2020 support?
proposed_answer: Chronic cool (22/11 degC) vs warm (32/22 degC, control) within each genotype x tissue: 18 contrasts (2 genotypes x 9 tissues). Inv4m vs B73-haplotype within a temperature is a genotype comparison, not a cold contrast.
evidence: phase = chronic for both chambers; temp_rank 1 = cool, control_temperature_C = 32; no time_h or recovery_h.

question: Eight libraries (B104 cold and control, 4 replicates each) are in PRJNA556806 but not in the paper: it describes 21 DH lines x 2 treatments x 4 replicates = 168 libraries (Table S1 lists exactly those). The accession note calls PE0075 and B104 'reference lines', but PE0075 is one of the 21 DH lines in the paper. Keep B104?
proposed_answer: Keep include = TRUE as genotype B104 (other inbred, cold_tolerance NR, cold vs control at 12 vs 18 °C, same design). Do not count it with the 21 DH lines in tolerant/susceptible groupings; confirm with the data owner (Hochholdinger lab) that B104 was grown and treated together with the DH lines.
evidence: BioSample aliases C11, C12, F11, F12, J15, J16, D15, D16 (runs SRR9841917, SRR9841918, SRR9841942, SRR9841959, SRR9841997, SRR9841998, SRR9842058, SRR9842059) are B104; Table S1 (BMC Genomics additional file 2) has 168 samples and no B104; B104 is not mentioned in the text.

item: Light or dark during the 8 h treatment
question: Methods: 10 seedlings per replicate grown 4 d at 26/18 °C (16 h light/8 h dark), then an 8 h treatment at 12 °C (cold) or 18 °C (control). The Discussion calls 12 vs 18 °C the cold vs control 'night temperatures'. Was the 8 h treatment in the dark (the 8 h night) or did it span light?
proposed_answer: Record temperature_C 12 / 18 (treatment temperatures), leave temperature_night_C and light_condition empty because the paper does not say. If the treatment was the night period, 18 °C equals the control night temperature of the growth regime.
evidence: Frey 2020 Methods 'Plant growth and RNA isolation' and Discussion 'Transcriptomic response upon cold treatment'.

question: The main text names only PE0161, PE0002 and PE0328 as the most tolerant lines; the tolerant/susceptible split of the 21 lines (11 tolerant, 10 susceptible) is in Fig. 1 (colours, not readable from text). I took it from the column grouping of Table S3 (Additional file 4: 'Susceptible genotypes' = PE0440 PE0159 PE0026 PE0420 PE0345 PE0334 PE0019 PE0022 PE0349 PE0323; 'Tolerant genotypes' = PE0265 PE0359 PE0075 PE0100 PE0040 PE0485 PE0055 PE0099 PE0002 PE0328 PE0161), which agrees with the 'sum tolerants' and 'sum susceptibles' columns and with the text. Check against Fig. 1b?
proposed_answer: Use the Table S3 grouping (tolerant 11, susceptible 10). Tolerance is the paper's root growth ratio cold/control (a continuous measure; the paper's classes are the two groups).
evidence: Table S3 header row, additional file MOESM4 of doi 10.1186/s12864-020-6682-1; text 'ten cold susceptible ... and eleven cold tolerant DH-lines'.

question: BioSample says 4 days after sowing; Methods say 4 d at control conditions then an 8 h treatment (so about 4.3 d at harvest). Which age to record?
proposed_answer: age_days = 4 (age at treatment start, as in BioSample); stage = 4 days after sowing.
evidence: BioSample attribute age; Methods.

question: Does PRJNA877073 belong to Friero et al. 2023 (Plant Sci 326:111525)? No data statement was readable (ScienceDirect blocked) and the BioProject lists no publication.
proposed_answer: Likely yes; accept with the status 'repository_match'. Confirm from the paper's data statement if possible.
evidence: BioProject 'Molecular signatures of temperature-dependent root meristem growth in young maize seedlings' (same title as the SSRN preprint of the paper); submitter Universidad Miguel Hernandez de Elche (paper authors Larriba, Justamante and Perez-Perez are at UMH Elche), funding Junta de Extremadura (authors Friero, Salguero and Alarcon, Extremadura); description: seedlings grown hydroponically at 30 C then cooled to 20 C for up to 24 h, total RNA from root tips, BGISEQ-500; abstract of the paper: root tips of young maize seedlings grown hydroponically at 30 C and cooled to 20 C, time-course transcriptomics. Run metadata: hybrid DKC 664, root, 'germinated seeds'.

question: How are the DR_x-y labels decoded?
proposed_answer: DR_<h>-<T>: h = hours after the shift from 30 C, T = temperature (C). Groups: 0 h at 30 C (control, time zero), 6 h at 30 C and at 20 C, 12 h at 30 C and at 20 C. Controls at 30 C are time-matched.
evidence: BioSample aliases 'DR6_h-20C_R2', 'DR12_h-30C_R3', 'DR0_h-30C_R1'; age attributes 24 h (h = 0), 30 h (h = 6), 36 h (h = 12) = 24 h + h; description of DR_6-20_R2 reads '30 hours root at 20C'. The paper's abstract says time-course up to 24 h, but the deposited groups stop at 12 h (no 24 h library).

question: Group DR_6-30 has only two libraries (R1, R2); every other group has three.
proposed_answer: Keep as deposited (14 libraries); no replicate R3 for the 6 h 30 C control.
evidence: ENA run list PRJNA877073: DR_6-30_R1 (SRR21494922), DR_6-30_R2 (SRR21494921); no R3 among the 14 runs.

question: SRR21494925 (DR_12-20_R2) has 12.9 M spots and SRR21494916 (DR_6-20_R2) 30.8 M, versus ~60-63 M for the other 12; both were released later (2022-10-12 vs 2022-09-12).
proposed_answer: Keep include = TRUE; check mapped counts at QC and consider the library-quality rule for these two.
evidence: ENA read_count PRJNA877073.

question: ENA/runs.tsv list the layout as PAIRED, but every run has a single FASTQ file and base_count = 100 x read_count (single 100-nt read per spot), while the BioProject says directional paired-end BGISEQ-500 with 100 cycles.
proposed_answer: Treat as single-end (one file per run) in the pipeline unless the FASTQ turns out to be interleaved; verify with the first reads.
evidence: runs.tsv fastq_urls single file per run; ENA base_count / read_count = 100.

question: BioSample ages are 24-36 h of seed germination (root tips of hydroponic seedlings); the paper calls them young seedlings.
proposed_answer: stage_class seed/germination (age_days 1-1.5, tissue_group Root). Reclassify to seedling if the project prefers.
evidence: BioSample 'age: 24/30/36 hours germinated seeds'; paper title 'roots of maize seedlings grown hydroponically at low temperature'.

question: Hydroponic medium, light regime, number of root tips pooled and exact tip length are not available in the run metadata.
proposed_answer: Leave empty; check the paper if needed.
evidence: BioSample attributes contain only cultivar, tissue, age, temperature and replicate.

question: The run metadata give only 'cold-treated_12h' and 'untreated_12h'; no temperature. The Molecular Plant paper is paywalled (no PMC, not open access in Europe PMC). Which temperatures were used?
proposed_answer: Sheet uses 4 C cold and 25 C control (numbers are required by the validator), assumed from the same CAU lab's other studies in this set (Jiang2022, Zeng2021, Zeng2024, Liao2026: 4 C vs 25 C, 12 h). Verify in the paper Methods (needs institutional access) before contrasts are built.
evidence: ENA PRJNA996745 study title 'RNA-Seq and DAP-Seq reveal HSF21 response genes in maize during cold sress'; experiment titles 'Maize leaf_<genotype>_cold-treated_12h#n' / '_untreated_12h#n'; Europe PMC record: isOpenAccess N, inPMC N.

item: replicate numbering of hsf21 cold libraries
question: SRR25345319 and SRR25345331 are both titled 'hsf21_cold-treated_12h#2'; no run is titled #1 (SRR25345330 is #3). Which is #1?
proposed_answer: Treated as three distinct libraries (different read counts: 29,684,944 vs 27,999,029) with arbitrary replicate numbers 1 (SRR25345319), 2 (SRR25345331), 3 (SRR25345330). The label error does not change the design (3 cold hsf21 libraries).
evidence: Run list of PRJNA996745; experiment titles of SRX21084729 and SRX21084717 are identical.

question: Is hsf21 a CRISPR knockout in the LH244 background? Run metadata give WT cultivar LH244 but only ecotype 'hsf21' for the mutant.
proposed_answer: Assumed LH244 background (CAU lines are made in LH244; WT control is LH244) and genotype_class mutant; cold_tolerance left NR (the abstract says HSF21 positively regulates cold tolerance but the mutant phenotype is not readable). Confirm in the paper.
evidence: BioSample SAMN36632544 (WT, cultivar LH244) and SAMN36632545 (hsf21, ecotype hsf21); PubMed abstract (PMID 39095994).

question: Titles of controls say 'untreated_12h'. Is the control a 12 h time-matched untreated sample or a time-zero sample?
proposed_answer: Treated as a single-point untreated control at 25 C (time_h empty). If the paper says the controls were kept at 25 C for 12 h alongside the cold samples, they are time-matched.
evidence: Experiment titles 'Maize leaf_WT_untreated_12h#1' etc.; Jiang2022 titles (same lab) lack '12h' on untreated samples.

question: Each of the five conditions has a single library. All contrasts are unreplicated.
proposed_answer: Kept as is (replicate = 1 for all); contrasts LT2 vs CK2 and LT3 vs CK3 (or LT3 vs LT2) will be display-only (no SE).
evidence: Methods 'RNA isolation and transcriptome sequencing': one RNA sample per condition; Table 1 lists five libraries.

question: CK0 is dry seed; the validator needs a numeric temperature. Recovery sample LT3 was sampled at 25 C after the 5 C step.
proposed_answer: CK0: phase control, temperature_C 25 (placeholder = control temperature), time_h 0; usable only as a non-time-matched baseline (the paper itself compares CK0 vs LT2). LT3: phase recovery, temperature_C 25, time_h 3, recovery_h 1; temp_rank 1 marks the group that had the 5 C step.
evidence: Methods 'Plant material'; Figure 1 legend 'LT2+LT3: dry seeds were soaked in water for 2 h at 5 C (LT2), and then transferred to 25 C for 1 h recovery (LT3)'.

question: Run titles only say 'RNA-Seq of Zea mays'; the condition comes from the BioSample alias.
proposed_answer: Mapping by BioSample alias (Imbibed Em-LT2, CK2, CK0, LT3, CK3 for SRR5028662-SRR5028666) and confirmed by the clean-read counts in Table 1 (18,371,393 / 14,837,739 / 20,872,802 / 19,648,277 / 17,392,295).
evidence: runs.tsv biosample_attributes; paper Table 1.

item: Meaning of CK, T, 72h, 120h, HF24h in run aliases
question: The paper never defines the aliases. Methods 4.4: 'MIL-IB030 and recurrent parent B73 were treated at 2 °C and 25 °C for 3 d (72 h) and 5 d (120 h), followed by recovery at 25 °C for 24 h, with three biological repeats' (2 genotypes x 6 groups x 3 replicates = 36). Are CK and T control (25 °C) and treatment (2 °C), the digit the replicate, and HF24h the 24 h recovery group?
proposed_answer: Yes: CK_72h and CK_120h = 25 °C controls matched to T_72h and T_120h (2 °C, 72 and 120 h); T_HF24h = cold-treated plants after 24 h recovery at 25 °C (HF read as pinyin huifu, 'recovery'); CK without suffix = 25 °C control for the HF24h group. Digits 1-3 are replicates.
evidence: Methods 4.1 and 4.4 of doi 10.3390/ijms24032629; run aliases in CNCB GSA CRA007319 (gsa_runs.tsv); no CK/T/HF labels in the paper text.

item: Cold duration before the recovery group
question: Only one recovery group per genotype (T_HF24h). Did the 24 h recovery follow the 3 d or the 5 d cold treatment (or were two recovery groups pooled)? Likewise what is the sampling time of plain CK: a time-zero control, or the control matched to the recovery sample?
proposed_answer: Unknown. time_h = NR for T_HF24h (recovery_h = 24) and for plain CK. If forced to choose: recovery after the 5 d (120 h) treatment (time_h 144), and plain CK as the control matched to the recovery sample; ask the corresponding authors (Sichuan Agricultural University) before using recovery contrasts.
evidence: Methods 4.1: 'After the treatments had been applied for 3 and 5 d and plants had recovered for 24 h, the leaves ... were frozen'.

question: The paper grades 21 MILs (MIL-IB030 highly cold-tolerant, MIL-IB021 highly cold-sensitive) but gives B73 no grade; it only says MIL-IB030 tolerated cold better than B73 (B73 leaf electrolyte leakage was intermediate between MIL-IB030 and the EMS mutants). Set B73 to sensitive?
proposed_answer: cold_tolerance = NR for B73 (comparison genotype, less tolerant than MIL-IB030 but not labelled). MIL-IB030 = tolerant.
evidence: Results 2.1-2.2 and Methods 4.1.

question: Temperatures 2 and 25 °C (constant, no day/night values given), illumination written as 3000 µmol m-2 s-1 (implausibly high for a growth chamber; to verify), photoperiod not reported; leaf position and exact seedling age not reported. Methods also mention a three-leaf and one-heart stage for the F2:3 QTL experiment, but RNA-seq plants were treated at the single-leaf stage.
proposed_answer: temperature_C 2 (cold) and 25 (control); light recorded as written with the caveat; stage = single-leaf stage, age_days empty.
evidence: Methods 4.1.

item: Sample counts and mapping to repository
question: 36 runs = 36 samples, one run per sample; each alias is unique (e.g. B73_CK1, B73_CK1_72h, B73_CK1_120h, B73_T1_72h ...). Anything missing?
proposed_answer: Nothing missing: 2 genotypes x 6 groups x 3 replicates = 36 matches the paper's '36 samples'.
evidence: gsa_runs.tsv (CRA007319), accessions_resolved.tsv.

question: Is PRJNA598312 (not the PRJNA306879 cited in the paper) the paper's seedling RNA-seq dataset, and do any PRJNA306879 runs belong to the cold series?
proposed_answer: Yes. Use the 18 PRJNA598312 seedling runs; none of PRJNA306879's 12 RNA-seq runs belongs to the cold series.
evidence: PRJNA598312 study title is 'Deletion of maize RDM4 results in disruptions to endosperm maturation, vegetative growth and the transcriptomic response to cold stress'; SRA experiment titles 'wild type leaf 1 at 28', '... at 10', '... at 2' match the paper's seedling28/seedling10/seedling2 and its '18 seedling samples + 6 endosperm samples'. PRJNA306879 RNA-seq runs (12) are BSR-seq pools of other mutants (1039-o2, 937, 916, 1115, 883, 1554 normal/mutant pools for mapping). Paper text cites only PRJNA306879.

question: seedling2 has 4 WT libraries (replicates 1-4) but only 2 rdm4 libraries (replicates 1-2); the other five groups have 3 each. Is one WT library mislabeled, or did the paper really use 4 WT and 2 mutant replicates?
proposed_answer: Keep labels as deposited (include = TRUE). After quantification check RDM4 (Zm00001d023237) in SRR10808181 (WT rep 4): the transcript is absent in rdm4. If absent, relabel it as rdm4 seedling2 rep 3.
evidence: BioSample aliases and SRA titles both say 'wild type leaf 4 at 2' (SRR10808181) and give mutant leaf 1 and 2 only at 2 C (SRR10808180, SRR10808179); the paper states 18 seedling samples without per-group replicate numbers (it says RDM4 transcript absent in mutant).

question: BioSample tissue is 'seedling'; the paper's Results say 'leaf' and Methods say 'seedling RNA'. Which tissue was sequenced?
proposed_answer: Leaf (tissue_group Leaf); leaf position and whether the whole seedling shoot was used are not stated.
evidence: Paper (accepted manuscript text): 'Transcriptomic analysis in leaf tissue confirmed that the expression of RDM4 was absent in the mutant'; 'DNA was extracted from leaves of ~14-day-old plants' for genotyping; BioSample attribute tissue = seedling.

question: seedling2 samples had 3 d at 10 C followed by 1 d at 2 C. How should time_h be defined?
proposed_answer: time_h = hours since first cold onset (10 C): 72 for seedling10, 96 for seedling2; seedling28 controls have empty time_h (single-point control). Contrast builder should treat seedling2 as a cumulative 10 C -> 2 C treatment (not an independent 2 C exposure).
evidence: Paper Methods: 'seedlings were grown at 28 C for 11 d, 10 C for 3 d followed by 2 C for 1 d'.

question: Controls (seedling28) are described as grown 14 d at 28 C in the greenhouse; cold groups were moved to a Conviron growth chamber. Is the control in the same environment?
proposed_answer: Unknown; keep as is and treat as a possible batch/environment difference between control and cold groups.
evidence: Paper Methods: 'germinating the seeds in standard potting compost in 3-inch peat pots, growing in the greenhouse and subsequently in a Conviron growth chamber. The seedling28 treatment consisted of 14 d growth at 28 C in the greenhouse (16 h day, 8 h night)'.

question: Number of plants pooled per sample, leaf stage, and time of day of sampling are not stated.
proposed_answer: Leave pooled_plants empty; stage given as 14-day-old seedling.
evidence: Paper Methods give only '14-day-old plants'; HiSeq 2500, PE125, University of Minnesota Genomics Center; wild type/mutant seedlings assigned by seed opaque phenotype and leaf DNA genotyping (WT = B73-background siblings).

question: BioSample says tissue 'leaf' for zmice1-1 and 'leaf, root' for WT (a BioSample shared with the ChIP-seq WT control); the catalogue says 'seedlings (organ NR)'. Which tissue was sequenced?
proposed_answer: Leaf for all 12 libraries (the zmice1-1 BioSample says leaf; the two genotypes must be the same tissue). The catalogue's Whole seedling is not used. Confirm in the paper.
evidence: BioSample SAMN23019720 (zmice1-1, leaf), SAMN23019719 (WT, 'leaf, root'; also holds the ChIP-seq WT run SRR16925112, excluded); catalogue row Jiang2022.

question: Cold 4 C for 12 h vs 25 C comes from a secondary summary (catalogue notes), not from the paper text, which could not be read (no PMC, nature.com blocked).
proposed_answer: Accepted as 4 C / 12 h vs 25 C; check Methods when the paper is accessible.
evidence: Run titles say '12h cold treated'; accessions_resolved note; PRJNA779257 study description 'compared cold-induced gene expression in wild-type maize and a zmice1 mutant'.

question: Untreated controls carry no time point. Time-matched 12 h controls or time-zero samples? Replicates are 3 per group (titles #1-#3).
proposed_answer: Treated as single-point untreated controls (time_h empty). Replicate numbers follow the '#n' in the SRA titles.
evidence: Experiment titles 'RNAseq untreated WT #1-3', 'RNAseq untreated zmice1-1 #1-3'.

question: Mutant background not stated; cold_tolerance not stated in the readable text.
proposed_answer: background LH244 (inferred from the paired WT); cold_tolerance NR.
evidence: BioSample attributes; PubMed abstract (PMID 36241735) does not give the mutant phenotype.

question: MC28/MC67 (6 libraries) are non-germinated dry seeds. Should they be used in any cold contrast?
proposed_answer: Keep include = TRUE but do not use as the control for 15 C germination (it confounds germination state with cold). The proper control is the 25 C germinated NT group (MN28, MN67). temperature_C = 25 is a placeholder required by the sheet format; other_factor_level 'dry seed (non-germinated)' marks them.
evidence: Paper Methods: 'Nongerminated dry seeds were used as control'; reported DEGs are MC vs ML (N28 16,017; N67 14,435) and ML67 vs ML28; no LT vs NT contrast reported. BioSample alias MC28_1..3 / MC67_1..3 with treatment 'control' and no temperature.

question: PRJNA911416's BioProject title is 'Genome sequencing and assembly' and the paper's PMC text had no data statement in the retrieved copy. Is this the paper's dataset?
proposed_answer: Yes, accept.
evidence: BioSample aliases MN28_1..3, MN67, MC28, MC67, ML28, ML67 match the paper's group names (MC28, ML28, MC67, ML67, ML67_vs_ML28); 18 libraries = 2 lines x 3 conditions x 3 reps as in the paper (18 samples, 148.09 Gb); accession harvested from the paper text (accessions_resolved).

question: N28 and N67 are waxy corn inbreds; the BioSample cultivar is 'Zea mays L. ceratina Kulesh' for all. Tolerance labels?
proposed_answer: genotype_class other inbred; N28 tolerant, N67 sensitive (the paper's labels).
evidence: Paper: 'N28, a low-temperature resistant waxy corn ... N67, a LT-sensitive waxy corn'.

question: Paper says 'Illumina HiSeq' without layout; ENA lists HiSeq 2000, PAIRED.
proposed_answer: Treat as paired-end per ENA; no action.
evidence: ENA run table PRJNA911416 (library_layout PAIRED).

question: Sampling is described as 3 d after the start of germination, when the N67 radicle broke through the coat at 15 C; was the 25 C group also sampled at 3 d?
proposed_answer: Assume yes (3 d for NT and LT).
evidence: Paper Methods: 'After 3 days of germination ... Each samples including 5 germinating seed were harvested for N28 and N67 under NT and LT conditions'.

question: SRP065916 holds 12 runs but the paper has 7 libraries (KR701 control x2 and freezing x1, Hei8834 control x2 and freezing x2). Five runs of the first submission (SRR2911073, SRR2911287, SRR2911288, SRR2911289, SRR2919276) have the same read counts and base counts as SRR3039751, SRR3039752, SRR3039753, SRR3039754 and SRR3039748 of a second submission (titled 'Maize freezing tolerance: Sample 3A, 5A, 7A, 9A, 12A'). Count them once?
proposed_answer: Yes. Keep SRR3039748-SRR3039754 (the complete set, 7 libraries, titled by paper sample number) and exclude the five first-deposit runs. The sheet has them as separate include = FALSE rows; add them to the duplicate exclusions in build_runs.py so they are not downloaded or quantified.
evidence: ENA run report: read_count pairs 10,146,508 / 12,918,221 / 11,238,002 / 11,131,723 / 11,476,212 occur twice each; n_bases equal; fastq MD5 differ. Paper: 'about 154.4 million sequencing reads', seven samples (Table 1 text: CT, CS, FS with two replicates, FT with one).

question: These two runs have no first-deposit alias, so their condition is not stated anywhere. Are they Hei8834 after freezing, replicates 1 and 2?
proposed_answer: Yes, by elimination: the other five libraries are identified by alias (CKTR1-2, CKSR1-2, FTR1), and the paper's remaining two libraries are the freezing-treated sensitive line (FS, two replicates). Replicate numbers 1 and 2 are arbitrary between them.
evidence: ENA run_alias values CKTR1, CKTR2, CKSR1, CKSR2, FTR1 (SRR2911073, SRR2911287, SRR2911288, SRR2911289, SRR2919276); SRR3039749 and SRR3039750 appear only in the second deposit (read counts 9,509,750 and 10,823,817 match no other run).

question: SRR2911288 and SRR2911289 sit in one SRA experiment with the same title 'control sensitive replicated 1' but have different read counts. Two replicates or two runs of one library?
proposed_answer: Two replicates (CKSR1 and CKSR2): their read counts equal those of the second-deposit runs for Sample 7A and 9A, which are separate experiments. Both Hei8834 control replicates are kept (as SRR3039753 and SRR3039754).
evidence: ENA run report: SRX1423663 contains SRR2911288 (11,238,002 reads) and SRR2911289 (11,131,723 reads); SRX1495290 and SRX1495291 hold the same counts.

item: single freezing replicate and baseline control
question: KR701 after freezing has one library; both controls are 0 h samples before freezing (-1 C for 1 h). Consequences for contrasts?
proposed_answer: KR701 freezing vs control is unreplicated on the freezing side (n = 1 vs 2). Controls are time-zero samples at 25/20 C (time_h = 0); freezing at -1 C for 1 h, time_h = 1.
evidence: Paper: 'one replicate (R1) of the tolerant line after freezing stress (FT) was retrieved'; Methods: leaves sampled at 0 h (prior to freezing) and after 1 h freezing.

item: 12 runs vs 10 libraries in the paper: ABA samples
question: The deposit has ABA-replicate1/2 (SRR3984835, SRR3984871) that the paper never mentions (it reports Control, Salinity, Drought, Heat, Cold, 10 libraries). Keep them?
proposed_answer: Kept as include = TRUE: ABA at the control temperature is a hormone-only treatment (spec example), tagged other_factor = hormone treatment; dose and duration are unknown. They are not part of a cold contrast.
evidence: ENA run_alias list for SRP080208; paper Table 1 and Results ('five samples (Control, Salinity, Drought, Heat, and Cold)').

question: These six libraries share the control with the cold sample but are other stresses. Include or exclude?
proposed_answer: Set include = FALSE (project convention: other stresses in multi-stress projects are left out; runs.tsv did not drop them because all 12 runs sit in one SRA experiment). Flip to TRUE if you want them kept; heat is phase 'chronic' only as a placeholder.
evidence: CLAUDE.md M2 note: 'Run rules leave out other stresses in multi-stress projects (heat, salt, UV, drought)'; runs.tsv has all 12 runs include = TRUE.

question: All 12 runs sit in one SRA experiment and one BioSample; only the run alias names the condition, and Control replicate 1 (SRR3984708) has the placeholder alias 'Transcriptomic data of maize'.
proposed_answer: Mapping by run alias; SRR3984708 is Control 1 because its read count (27,238,880 pairs; x2 = 54,477,760) equals Table 1 Control replicate 1 and no other control run remains. All other aliases agree with Table 1 raw reads.

question: Each of the 12 cold-series and control libraries has two runs under the same BioSample: SRR12214964-984 (deposited 2020-07, the original set) and SRR12247895-915 (deposited 2021-08-25), with identical read counts (the first set's heat library MHT2 is truncated, 4.2 M vs 22.0 M reads, so the second set looks like a corrected full re-upload). Are they duplicates or independent sequencing of the same libraries?
proposed_answer: Duplicates of the same libraries (paper reports 21 libraries; the BioProject has 42 runs). Keep the 12 runs of the first set as the samples; the 12 SRR122478xx-9xx runs are listed as separate rows with include = FALSE (sample_id suffix _dup). Mark them as duplicates in build_runs.py so they are not downloaded.
evidence: runs.tsv: same biosample and identical n_spots for all 21 pairs except MHT2; ENA first_public 2020-07-15/21 vs 2021-08-25; paper: 21 samples (7 temperatures x 3)

item: temperature of control and growth regime
question: Paper writes 'growth chamber (25/22 C day/light cycle)'; are 25/22 C day/night temperatures, and what is the photoperiod? Controls are labelled NT at 25 C.
proposed_answer: Treat 25 C as the control temperature (as the paper does for NT); leave temperature_night_C and light_condition empty because the paper does not give them.
evidence: Methods 2.1 (PMC7464670)

question: Eight uniform seedlings were retained per pot and the second leaf of each seedling 'in each plot' was pooled as one replicate, but the number of leaves pooled per library is not stated.
proposed_answer: Leave pooled_plants empty (up to 8).
evidence: Methods 2.1 (PMC7464670)

question: All WT runs share BioSample SAMN22964617 and all mutant runs SAMN22964618 (alias just 'WT' / 'mutant'); groups and replicates come only from the ENA/SRA experiment titles. Are the titles reliable?
proposed_answer: Accept the experiment titles: WT 0 h, WT 4 C 12 h, WT 25 C 12 h, mutant 0 h, mutant 4 C 12 h, 3 replicates each (15 libraries).
evidence: ENA experiment_title for SRR16844559-73, e.g. 'WT leaf at 4 degree for 12 h-3', 'WT leaf at 25 degree for 12 h-1', 'Untreated mutant leaf-2'; paper Methods list exactly these five groups with three replicates.

question: The paper states a CRISPR/Cas9 loss-of-function bzip68-1 line compared with LH244 WT but (in the retrieved text) not the transformation background; the BioSample for the mutant gives only 'ecotype zmbzip68'.
proposed_answer: background LH244 for both genotypes; flag as inferred. Confirm from the paper's Materials section or ask the authors.
evidence: PMC9338793 web page (PubMed full-text tool returned an empty body; summary from the PMC page): WT = inbred LH244; bzip68-1 = CRISPR/Cas9 homozygous mutant without Cas9 transgene; other lines (bzip68-2, overexpression, teosinte) not used for RNA-seq. Mutant allele deletion size per that summary is 169 bp (verify).

question: There is no 25 C 12 h control for the mutant and no mutant 0 h vs WT 0 h batch control beyond the 0 h samples.
proposed_answer: Cold contrasts: WT 4 C 12 h vs WT 0 h (time-zero) and vs WT 25 C 12 h (time-matched, preferred); mutant 4 C 12 h vs mutant 0 h only.
evidence: Paper: WT kept at 25 C for 12 h 'to exclude circadian effects'; no equivalent group for the mutant.

question: Number of plants per sample and the clock time of sampling relative to the light cycle are not stated.
proposed_answer: Leave pooled_plants empty.
evidence: PMC page summary: 'The article does not state how many plants were pooled per sample'.

question: The bzip68-1 mutant is more cold tolerant than WT.
proposed_answer: cold_tolerance tolerant for bzip68-1, NR for LH244.
evidence: Paper abstract: bZIP68 'negatively regulates cold tolerance in maize'.

question: Eight dry-seed embryo libraries (CK-0, 4 genotypes x 2 reps) have no temperature condition; they are a non-germination control. How should they be used?
proposed_answer: include = FALSE (any Cold-15 vs CK-0 contrast would measure germination, not cold). temperature_C = 25 and phase = control are placeholders required by the validator. Set include = TRUE only if a germination baseline is wanted.
evidence: Results 2.2 (PMC9002958)

question: The SRA text says 'Seedling of 15 days after germination'; the paper defines Cold-15 as seeds germinated at 10 C for 15 d (days after sowing, DAS) and CK-3 as 25 C for 3 d.
proposed_answer: Use the paper's definition (15 d and 3 d after sowing); age_days = 15 and 3.
evidence: Results 2.1/2.2 and Methods 4.2/4.3 (PMC9002958)

question: Light conditions for the paper-roll cultures are not reported (the emergence test was in a dark chamber).
proposed_answer: Leave light_condition empty.
evidence: Methods 4.2 (PMC9002958)

question: Cold-15 (10 C) and CK-3 (25 C) are both germination-from-sowing conditions; CK-3 is entered as phase chronic (not control) following the spec's 'chronic cool vs chronic warm'.
proposed_answer: Contrast Cold-15 vs CK-3 within each genotype. Cold-15 vs CK-3 is time-confounded (15 vs 3 d) by design, matched on developmental stage by the authors.
evidence: Results 2.2 (PMC9002958)

question: Paper Results say RNA-seq sampling at 0/24 h; Methods say 0, 24 and 48 h. Which times are in GSE299259?
proposed_answer: 0, 24 and 48 h at 4 C, 3 replicates each for B73 and zmzfp69 (18 libraries).
evidence: GEO/SRA titles of the 18 runs: 'CK(B73),leaf,4°C,0h|24h|48h 1-3' and 'zmzfp69 (B73) mutant,leaf,4°C,0h|24h|48h 1-3'; paper Methods: 'treated at low temperature for 0 h, 24 h, and 48 h'.

question: There is no separate 25 C time-matched control; the 0 h samples (25 C before cold) are the only controls.
proposed_answer: Treat 0 h as the control (phase control, time_h 0, temperature_C 25). Cold effect = 24 h or 48 h vs 0 h within genotype, which also includes any circadian/age effect over 24-48 h.
evidence: Paper: 'The leaves ... of the mutant (zmzfp69) and control (B73) maize inbred lines were treated at low temperature for 0 h, 24 h, and 48 h'; GEO titles carry '4°C' even for 0 h.

question: BioSample genotype for the mutant reads 'ZmZFP69 knock down' and the field 'cell line' 'ZmZFP69(B73) knock down', but the paper describes a homozygous mutant with a 127-bp deletion and premature stop. How was it made and is it B73-background?
proposed_answer: genotype_class mutant, background B73 (from the GEO title 'zmzfp69 (B73) mutant'); the paper does not state how the mutant was generated.
evidence: Paper Results 2.1.1: 'this mutant had a 127-base deletion ... premature termination'; Methods: 'mutant (zmzfp69) and control (B73) maize inbred lines'.

question: The mutant is more cold tolerant than the control; B73 is not labelled as sensitive in the paper.
proposed_answer: cold_tolerance tolerant for zmzfp69, NR for B73.
evidence: Paper abstract: 'zmzfp69 homozygous mutant maize inbred line exhibited enhanced low-temperature tolerance compared to the control'.

item: photoperiod during cold and reference genome
question: Light conditions during the 4 C treatment are not stated (Methods give 16/8 h before cold and 12/12 h for the 24 h recovery after the phenotype test).
proposed_answer: Leave light_condition as described; no action needed for the sheet.
evidence: Paper Methods 4.1.1. The paper aligned to B73 v4 (HISAT2) per its text; RNA-seq read length not given (ENA: PE, NovaSeq 6000).

question: PRJDB41168 has no paper link, no title or author field matching the paper, and the paper's data statement was not read. Does the run metadata support that it belongs to Liao et al., Nature 2026?
proposed_answer: Yes, with moderate-to-high confidence: (1) the DDBJ BioProject, a mirror of CNCB PRJCA041350, is titled 'RNA-Seq of maize leaf in wild-type (LH244) and nla mutant under cold treatment' and describes 14-day-old LH244 and 'zmnla' seedlings at 25 or 4 C for 12 h, which is the paper's genotype, gene (NLA) and treatment; (2) provider China Agricultural University, the paper's institution (Yang Shuhua lab, which also deposited Gao2024, Jiang2022, Zeng2021, Zeng2024 in LH244); (3) NGDC release date 2025-11-10, before the paper's online date (25 Feb 2026); (4) 3 reps x 2 genotypes x 2 temperatures = 12 libraries as in the catalogue. Not confirmed: the paper's own data statement.
evidence: runs.tsv attributes (ngdc_project_id PRJCA041350, ngdc_release_date 2025-11-10, biomaterial_provider China Agricultural University, cultivar LH244); ENA PRJDB41168 study title/description; PubMed record PMID 41741638 (Nature 653:831-839, first author Huan Liao, CAU); accessions_resolved note 'submitter blank, ownership to confirm'.

question: Is the sequenced nla line the knockout or the engineered nla-delta12 allele? Which growth substrate, photoperiod and phosphate regime?
proposed_answer: Not determinable from the run metadata. Recorded as genotype 'nla', class mutant, background LH244; growth conditions NR. Check the paper (Methods, Extended Data) when accessible.
evidence: Abstract: NLA promotes JAZ11 degradation; 'nla-delta12' is an edited allele; BioProject says 'zmnla mutant'.

question: Is the 25 C control time-matched (kept 12 h at 25 C) or a time-zero sample?
proposed_answer: Treated as a single-point 25 C control (time_h empty); cold time_h = 12 from the BioProject description.
evidence: Sample titles WT-25C-n / nla-25C-n; BioProject description 'treated at 25 C or 4 C for 12 hours'.

question: What is HL-..-CK? The paper defines only CK (control), MD/SD, HT1h-HT24h and LT1h-LT24h; 'HL' is never defined, but there are two control sets (CK-L/R and HL-L/R-CK, 3 replicates each per tissue), and 84 libraries = 6 HL-CK + 30 HT + 30 LT + 6 CK + 12 drought. Is HL-CK the control for cold?
proposed_answer: Both sets are BioSample 'Normal' B73 leaf/root controls at 26/22 °C, so both are kept include = TRUE as phase control. Likely meaning: HL = high/low temperature, a control shared by the heat and cold time courses (isolate numbers B73-1..6 come directly before the heat series B73-7..36 and cold series B73-37..66), and CK (B73-67..72) = drought control (comes directly before the drought series B73-73..84). Proposal for contrasts: use HL-CK as the primary control for LT samples; CK as an alternative or additional control (check by PCA/correlation that HL-CK and CK agree before pooling them into 6 controls per tissue).
evidence: BioSample aliases and isolate numbers (SAMN54298994..SAMN54298999 = HL-CK, SAMN54299060..SAMN54299065 = CK); Liu 2026 Fig. 6 legend 'CK, control' only; Methods: 'Control plants were maintained at 26 °C/22 °C'; ENA project and BioSample records have no further description.

question: The paper has one control set per tissue (3 replicates) for five cold time points; controls are not time-matched, and the sampling time of the controls (and the time of day of the cold samplings) is not stated. Should contrasts treat controls as time-matched?
proposed_answer: No time-matched controls: time_h left empty for controls (single-point controls); LT samples compared with the single control per tissue, flagged as not time-matched in contrasts.
evidence: Methods 2.1: 'Control plants were maintained at 26 °C/22 °C (day/night). Tissue samplings were performed at 1-, 3-, 6-, 12-, and 24-hours post-treatment.'

item: Light during the cold treatment and time of day
question: Not stated whether cold treatment started at a particular time of day or whether the lights were kept on in the 4 °C chamber.
proposed_answer: light_condition records only the growth photoperiod (14/10 h); temperature_night_C left empty for cold samples (4 °C stated as a single value).
evidence: Methods 2.1 'seedlings were exposed to 40 °C (heat) or 4 °C (cold) for 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 hours'.

question: The 42 included runs are the cold series (30), CK (6) and HL-CK (6); heat (HT, 30) and drought (MD, SD, 12) runs are excluded in runs.tsv. Heat series and drought series share controls with the cold series if HL-CK/CK are shared controls.
proposed_answer: Nothing to change; just note that excluding the heat and drought runs does not remove any control needed for the cold contrasts.
evidence: runs.tsv exclude_reason (heat or drought treatment, no cold contrast).

question: The Ds-insertion mutant zmsrc2l2 was phenotyped (3 d cold) but all RNA-seq libraries are B73 (BioSample cultivar B73, isolates B73-1..84). Any mutant libraries hidden in the run set?
proposed_answer: No: all 84 runs are B73; no mutant samples to curate.
evidence: BioSample attributes cultivar/isolate for all 84 runs.

question: All 84 BioSamples have collection_date 2025-07-09 although time courses cannot all have been sampled that day; the date likely marks submission or the experiment start.
proposed_answer: Ignore collection_date; no batch information is recoverable from it.
evidence: BioSample attribute collection_date.

question: Zea mays ssp. mexicana accession '8493' is quantified in the paper against a de novo Trinity assembly, not B73. Reads will be mapped to B73 v5 here.
proposed_answer: Keep (genotype_class teosinte); expect lower mapping rates than B73-derived lines, so the library QC rules (mapping rate, per-genotype median) may flag these libraries. Not a sheet issue.
evidence: Paper Methods: paired reads mapped to an assembled reference (Trinity); catalogue notes 'teosinte, flag'.

question: Drought1/Drought2 (PEG 20%, 3 h) are other-stress libraries sharing the control.
proposed_answer: include = FALSE (project convention: other stresses are left out; runs.tsv did not drop them). Flip to TRUE if you want them kept.
evidence: CLAUDE.md M2 note on run rules; runs.tsv has all 6 runs include = TRUE.

question: Two biological replicates per treatment (>= 3 seedlings pooled; the paper also speaks of two replicated runs per sample, but GEO lists one library per replicate). The control is an untreated CK sample with no stated time point.
proposed_answer: Two replicates per group, one library each; control treated as a single-point 25 C control (time_h empty).
evidence: Methods: 'Two replicates for each treatment were applied and plant materials from at least three seedlings were pooled for each sample'; GEO sample titles CK1, CK2, Cold1, Cold2, Drought1, Drought2.

item: heat runs wrongly included in runs.tsv
question: Six heat libraries (B73_heat_R1-R3: SRR1238715, SRR1819196, SRR1819198; B37_heat_R1-R3: SRR1685982, SRR1819622, SRR1819624) are include = TRUE in runs.tsv although heat runs are meant to be excluded. The rule in build_runs.py uses the regex '_(heat|salt|UV)\b', which does not match when the alias continues with _R1-_R3 (underscore is a word character); only the unreplicated Oh43_heat/salt/UV and the B73/B37 salt and UV runs were excluded.
proposed_answer: Fix the regex (e.g. '_(heat|salt|UV)(_|$)') and rebuild runs.tsv; the 6 runs become include = FALSE (18 included runs remain). Meanwhile the 6 heat samples are listed here with include = FALSE and phase = chronic as a placeholder.
evidence: runs.tsv rows for these accessions have include TRUE with no exclude_reason; Methods: heat 50 C for 4 h

question: The SRA aliases name B73, B37 and Oh43. Makarevitch2015 uses B73, Mo17 and Oh43 and never mentions B37. The 11 libraries labelled B37 have exactly the layout the paper gives for Mo17 (3 control, 3 cold, 3 heat, 1 salt, 1 UV), and no Mo17 libraries exist in PRJNA244661 (27 BioSamples = 11 B73 + 11 'B37' + 5 Oh43 = the 27 libraries computed from the Methods). Are the 'B37' libraries really B37, or Mo17 mislabelled? Waters2017 lists B37 among its inbreds and cites this BioProject.
proposed_answer: Keep genotype = B37 (repository label) for now and flag it; genotype_class is 'other inbred' either way, so B73-only filters are unaffected. Check the corrected S1 Table (erratum PMC4599801) or the Waters2017 methods.
evidence: BioSample SAMN02727923 (sample name B37_cold_R1, cultivar B37_cold_R1); accessions_resolved.tsv; Methods (PMC4287451)

question: The erratum (PMC4599801) says the SRA numbers in the original S1 Table were wrong and replaces S1 Table (XLSX, not read). Run-to-sample mapping here uses the SRA submitter aliases (B73_cold_R1 ...), not the corrected S1 Table.
proposed_answer: Accept the SRA aliases; verify against the corrected S1 Table if a library looks odd after quantification.
evidence: accessions_resolved.tsv note; erratum PMC4599801

question: Oh43_control (SRR1238724, SRR1663702, SRR1663704) and Oh43_cold (SRR1663695, SRR1663696, SRR1663701) each have three runs under one BioSample with very different read counts (about 10 M and two of about 30 M pairs). Are they one library sequenced repeatedly or technical replicates?
proposed_answer: One sample per condition with all three runs (to be summed); Oh43 has no biological replicate, so its contrasts are unreplicated.
evidence: runs.tsv: same biosample, experiments SRX517450/SRX768760/SRX768761 and SRX517451/SRX768762/SRX768763

question: The libraries are whole above-ground tissue of 14-day-old seedlings (roots not sampled). Spec has Shoot (whole shoot) and Whole seedling.
proposed_answer: Shoot (whole above-ground seedling). Change to Whole seedling if that group should mean any whole-seedling sample.
evidence: Methods: 'Whole above ground tissue was collected for 14 day old seedlings'

question: Methods give both 'six seedlings were pooled together for each sample' (growth section) and 'eight plants pooled for each of the replicates' (RNA section).
proposed_answer: Leave pooled_plants empty.
evidence: Methods (PMC4287451)

question: Replicates of B73 and B37 were grown 3 d apart (R1, R2, R3 are separate plantings) and R1 libraries have much lower depth (8.6-17.7 M pairs) than R2/R3 (32-51 M), i.e. different sequencing batches.
proposed_answer: Add replicate as a blocking factor for the B73 and B37 cold vs control contrasts.
evidence: Methods; runs.tsv n_spots

question: Which of these runs are Waters2017's additions? Waters2017 cites PRJNA244661 and adds B37 (and PH207) to B73, Mo17 and Oh43; no PH207 libraries exist here.
proposed_answer: All runs are curated once under Makarevitch2015 (also_used_by Waters2017); only the B37-labelled libraries could be Waters2017's own, and that is unconfirmed (see the B37 vs Mo17 item).
evidence: accessions_resolved.tsv; Europe PMC abstract of Waters2017

item: recovery design: temperature and rank fields
question: RNA was sampled after 13 C for 4 d plus 25 C for 2 d, not at the end of the cold phase. How are temperature_C and temp_rank_in_study set?
proposed_answer: phase = recovery, time_h = 144 (96 h cold + 48 h recovery), recovery_h = 48; temperature_C = 25 (the temperature at sampling); temp_rank 1 for the cold-treated (LNT) group and 2 for the 25 C control, so rank marks which group had the cold step. The 13 C step is recorded only in curation_note and stage. Change if contrasts need the cold temperature as a field.
evidence: Methods: 'germination boxes were placed in a growth chamber at 13 C for 4 days followed by 25 C for 2 days (LNT) ... 25 C for 4 days (NT)'; BioSample dev_stage text.

question: LNT seedlings are 6 d old, NT controls 4 d old at sampling (same accumulated temperature by design). Is a developmental-stage confound acceptable?
proposed_answer: Keep as the authors designed it; flag as 'not age-matched' for contrasts. No cold-only (13 C end of cold) sample exists, so a cold contrast cannot be built.
evidence: Methods and Introduction: NT = 25 C for 4 days; LNT = 13 C for 4 days then 25 C for 2 days; 'similar accumulated temperature'.

question: All tissues of the germinating seed/seedling were pooled; tissue_group Seed/germination fits the vocabulary but the 6-day LNT samples are young seedlings.
proposed_answer: Seed/germination for all 12 (catalogue's choice).
evidence: Methods: 'All tissues of the two inbred lines under NT and LNT were used for RNA extraction'; BioSample tissue 'plant'.

question: The paper's Methods could not be read (Wiley page refused). The 48 runs fall into four BioProjects of 12 libraries each, named <condition><day>d_<rep>: PRJNA1088921 = CT (control) 5d/7d/11d/19d x 3 reps, PRJNA1088971 = S (stress) x same, PRJNA1126396 = CT x same, PRJNA1126430 = S x same. Is this 2 cultivars x 2 conditions (control, stress) x 4 days x 3 replicates?
proposed_answer: Yes: 4 projects x 4 days x 3 reps = 48 independent libraries (read counts all differ, so no run is a duplicate). Written as one sample per run: set A = PRJNA1088921 + PRJNA1088971, set B = PRJNA1126396 + PRJNA1126430.
evidence: ENA library_name per run (ENA Portal API read_run); ENA study descriptions: PRJNA1126396/PRJNA1126430 'two maize hybrids, one sensitive and one tolerant ... during compound stress and after recovery'

item: BioSample reuse and genotype of set B
question: PRJNA1088971, PRJNA1126396 and PRJNA1126430 all point to the same 12 BioSamples (SAMN40517247-SAMN40517258, aliases S1-S12, cultivar 'jidan 558', tissue 'seed'), although they hold different libraries (S libraries in two projects, CT libraries in the third). Set A (PRJNA1088921, own BioSamples; PRJNA1088971, S1-S12 as the original S libraries) is labelled jidan 558 (JD558, the sensitive hybrid). Set B's genotype is therefore not recorded anywhere.
proposed_answer: Set A = JD558 (hybrid, sensitive) from the BioSample cultivar. Set B left as genotype NR / genotype_class NR / cold_tolerance NR. Likely answer: set B = JD441 (the CHS-tolerant hybrid, 24 libraries), since the study used exactly these two hybrids and set A is JD558; confirm with the authors or the paper's Methods/Table of samples, then set genotype = JD441, genotype_class = hybrid, background = JD441, cold_tolerance = tolerant for all 24 setB rows.
evidence: runs.tsv biosample column (same 12 BioSamples under three BioProjects); abstract: 'Jidan441 (JD441, CHS-resistant) and Jidan558 (JD558, CHS-sensitive)'; companion paper PMID 39731983 (JD558 = cold- and high humidity-sensitive hybrid, JD441 = tolerant hybrid)

item: stress arm is combined cold + high moisture only
question: Libraries are 'S' (stress) vs 'CT' (control); the project title is 'maize seed of cold and high hummity combined stress'. The abstract describes three treatments (cold alone, high moisture alone, combined), but no cold-only (4 C at 15%) or moisture-only (20/15 C at 25%) libraries are in the repository. So every S vs CT contrast mixes cold with high soil moisture.
proposed_answer: Keep all 48 samples include = TRUE, with other_factor = soil moisture (control 15%, stress 25%). Treat S as CHS. Contrasts should be labelled combined cold + high moisture; I suggest keeping them out of pooled cold-only estimates unless Rubén decides otherwise (the temperature effect cannot be separated from the moisture effect).
evidence: Library names and project title; abstract (PubMed 39887997); ENA study description of PRJNA1126396

question: The two abstracts do not agree on the timeline. Physiol Plant abstract: 5-day cold (4 C), 25% moisture and the combination 'were initiated at sowing, followed by a return to normal growth conditions (20 C light/15 C dark, 15%) at 7 DAS'; transcript and metabolite differences are highlighted 'at 7 DAS', and recovery measurements come after removal. Companion paper (Plant Physiol Biochem 2024): stress 'at sowing ... for five days'. Library day labels are 5d, 7d, 11d, 19d. Does the cold start at sowing (day 0) and end at 5 DAS or at 7 DAS, and are the days counted from sowing?
proposed_answer: Written on the Physiol Plant abstract: day suffix = days after sowing; cold begins at sowing, so time_h = day x 24 (120, 168, 264, 456) for both CT and S; S5d and S7d = phase cold (4 C, 25% moisture); S11d and S19d = recovery at 20/15 C and 15% moisture with recovery_h = 96 and 288 (4 and 12 d after 7 DAS); CT = control at 20 C (night 15 C), time-matched. If cold ended at 5 DAS, S7d is recovery (recovery_h 48), S11d 144 and S19d 336; if the 5-day stress started after 2 d, time_h shifts by 48 h. Needs the paper's Methods; until then treat the 7d samples as uncertain between cold and recovery.
evidence: PubMed abstracts of 39887997 and 39731983; ENA library names

question: BioSample tissue is 'embryo' for the 12 CT libraries of PRJNA1088921 but 'seed' for the S libraries (and for the reused BioSamples of set B), while the abstract and project titles say 'seed'. Were different tissues sampled for control and stress, or is this a labelling inconsistency?
proposed_answer: Both are tissue_group = Seed/germination. tissue_detail repeats each BioSample's value (embryo for set A CT, seed otherwise); po_term left empty. Assume the same tissue for CT and S, but confirm in the Methods because an embryo vs whole-seed difference would confound the CT vs S contrasts of set A.
evidence: runs.tsv biosample_attributes: PRJNA1088921 tissue 'embryo', dev_stage 'germination period'; PRJNA1088971, PRJNA1126396, PRJNA1126430 tissue 'seed'

question: Only the normal regime (20 C during light, 15 C during dark, 15% gravimetric water content) and the stress (4 C; 25% water content) are given in the abstract. The stress night temperature, photoperiod, container, substrate, seed number per library and whether the control used the same normal regime from sowing are not reported.
proposed_answer: temperature_C = 20 (night 15) for CT and recovery, 4 for stress (night empty), control_temperature_C = 20; light_condition and pooled_plants left empty; growth_system says details not reported. temp_rank_in_study: 4 C = 1, 20 C = 2.
evidence: Abstract (PubMed 39887997)

question: The paper labels JD441 'CHS-resistant' and JD558 'CHS-sensitive', i.e. tolerance to the combined cold + high moisture stress, not necessarily to cold alone.
proposed_answer: Used the paper's labels (JD558 sensitive; JD441 tolerant once set B is confirmed) with the caveat that the label refers to the combined stress.
evidence: Abstract (PubMed 39887997); companion paper abstract (PubMed 39731983, 'cold- and high humidity-sensitive hybrid')

question: runs.tsv has empty alias/title and identical SRA titles for all 15 runs. How were runs assigned to condition and replicate?
proposed_answer: From the NCBI BioSample records SAMN47625728-SAMN47625742 (sample names control_1-5, mild_cold_1-5, severe_cold_1-5), mapped via the run's BioSample accession.
evidence: BioSample page SAMN47625728 (control_1, rep1, temperature 22, root hair, B73, age 4 days, treatment control); the other 14 read from a single efetch listing; SAMN47625736 (mild_cold_4, rep4, temp 12) re-checked individually. ENA run table gives no sample alias.

question: Methods say ~120-150 seedlings per replicate, Results say 120.
proposed_answer: pooled_plants left empty (range in curation_note).
evidence: PMC12452017 Methods ('approximately 120-150 seedlings constituted a pooled biological replicate') and Results ('each pooled from 120 seedlings').

question: Treatments are 24 h at 27/22 (control), 16/12 (mild) or 10/6 (severe) day/night. Single time point.
proposed_answer: temperature_C = day value, temperature_night_C = night value; time_h = 24 for cold samples, empty for the single-point controls.
evidence: Paper Methods: control 27 C/22 C, mild 16 C/12 C, severe 10 C/6 C, 16 h light/8 h dark, 3-d-old seedlings treated for 24 h.

question: The paper also describes a recovery (24 h severe cold then control) used only for root diameter and root hair measurements.
proposed_answer: No RNA-seq libraries from it; nothing to add.
evidence: Paper Methods: root diameter measurement; RNA-seq section lists only control, mild and severe cold (15 libraries).

question: Neither the paper nor the BioSample names the maize line or cultivar.
proposed_answer: genotype, genotype_class and background = NR. The sheet cannot be filtered to B73; the dataset stays out of any B73-only pooling.
evidence: BioSample attributes (alias, isolate 'cold stress Nh', tissue leaf, age 3 weeks) have no cultivar field; Methods say only 'seedlings of 11 selected representative angiosperm species'.

question: BioSample age is '3 weeks' for the maize samples, but the Methods give three weeks only for Arabidopsis and 'young seedlings growing up to ~30 cm' for the other species.
proposed_answer: age_days = 21 from the BioSample (primary source), stage text records both statements; stage_class seedling.
evidence: BioSample age '3 weeks'; Methods 'Plant materials and growth conditions'.

question: BioSample alias is 'Zm-L<h>h_rep1' for all three runs of a time point; the three replicates are separate runs.
proposed_answer: Replicate numbers from the ENA run_alias (Zm-L<h>h_rep<n>-1.fq.gz) for each run.
evidence: ENA run report PRJNA767196: e.g. SRR17200351 Zm-L24h_rep1, SRR17200350 Zm-L24h_rep2, SRR17200349 Zm-L24h_rep3.

question: The only control is the 0 h sample at 25 C (no 2/24/168 h warm controls); cold-treatment starts were staggered so harvest was on the same day.
proposed_answer: time_h = 0 for the controls, 2/24/168 for cold. Contrasts are cold time point vs 0 h; the control is not age-matched at 168 h (7 d).
evidence: Methods 'Cold stress treatment': the 168 h group was moved to 4 C a week before harvest, then the 24, 2 and 0 h groups at proper times.

item: temperature_C for local and distal samples (GSE167881)
question: Under shoot-only (4S26R) and root-only (26S0R) chilling, only one organ is cold. Should temperature_C, phase and temp_rank describe the chilled site (treatment arm) or the sampled organ's own temperature (leaf in 26S0R and root in 4S26R were at 26 C)?
proposed_answer: Written as the treatment arm: temperature_C = 4 (whole plant, shoot only) or 0 (root only), phase = cold, time_h = 24, other_factor = chilling site with the level in other_factor_level; the sampled organ's own temperature and local/distal status are in curation_note. Local response = tissue matches the chilled site (leaf in 4S26R, root in 26S0R, both in 4S4R); distal = tissue not chilled (root in 4S26R, leaf in 26S0R). If the contrast builder wants organ temperature instead, distal samples would be 26 C and phase would need a decision.
evidence: GSE167881 treatment strings: whole-plant chilling (4 C shoot + 4 C root), shoot-only chilling (4 C shoot + 26 C root), root-only chilling (26 C shoot + 0 C root), each for 24 hours; 26 C shoot + 26 C root = normal condition (control)

question: Top-crown and bottom-crown were taken from a ~7 mm crown segment. In 4S26R the crown 'was at 4 C (chilled air temperature) but close to the 26 C water bath'; in 26S0R it 'was at 26 C (air temperature), but close to the 0 C iced water' and was not submerged. The paper applies local/distal only to leaves and roots.
proposed_answer: Keep crowns in the sheet with other_factor_level = chilling site as written and do not call them local or distal; contrasts should use crowns only for whole-plant vs control (4S4R) unless Rubén decides how to treat the partial exposure. Tissue_group = Shoot; po_term left empty (no obvious Plant Ontology term for crown halves).
evidence: Xue 2021 JXB Methods and Results (OUP page read via WebFetch; PMC full text not available)

question: Root-only chilling used roots submerged in iced water (0 C). The spec defines freezing as <= 0 C; this is chilling (the paper's wording, no freezing of the tissue reported), and measured root and crown temperatures are not reported.
proposed_answer: Treat as chilling at 0 C (nominal), not freezing; temp_rank_in_study = 1 for 26S0R, 2 for the 4 C arms, 3 for 26 C. Do not use these samples for freezing/acclimation analyses.
evidence: Paper Methods: pots 'placed into a polystyrene foam box containing iced water to submerge the roots'; GEO treatment string 26 C shoot + 0 C root

question: The paper says 3' RNA-seq used three biological replicates with 9 seedlings pooled per replicate, but GSE167156 has 2 libraries per line x condition (16 runs = 4 lines x 2 conditions x 2 reps), while GSE167881 has 3 (48 runs). Was a third replicate not deposited, or did GSE167156 use 2 replicates?
proposed_answer: Keep the 2 deposited replicates per group (pooled_plants = 9 from the paper's general statement); contrasts from GSE167156 have n = 2 vs 2. A third replicate would have to come from the authors.
evidence: GSE167156: GSM5098154-GSM5098169, 16 samples (rep1, rep2 only); paper Methods: 'each of three biological replicates pooled tissue from nine seedlings'

item: chilling duration and time-matching for GSE167156
question: GEO sample records for GSE167156 give 26 C for control and 4 C for chilling but no duration. The paper states leaf RNA-seq for the four-line comparison was done after 24 h at 4 C. It is not stated whether controls were sampled at the same time of day or after the same 24 h.
proposed_answer: time_h = 24 for the 4 C samples; control time_h left empty (single time point, not a time course). Treat controls as time-matched at 26 C.
evidence: GEO GSM5098154 treatment protocol '26 C for control, 4 C for chilling treatment'; paper Methods 'Leaf RNA-seq for the four-line comparison was done after 24 h at 4 C' (OUP page)

item: light during chilling and start time
question: Growth before treatment was 26 C, 14 h/10 h day/night, 250 umol m-2 s-1, 50-70% humidity. Tissues were collected at 11:00 h; the paper does not say when chilling started or whether the 4 C chamber (and the 26 C water bath or iced-water set-ups) had light.
proposed_answer: light_condition records the pre-treatment regime and notes light during chilling as not reported; no further detail available.
evidence: GEO growth protocol; paper Methods (sampling at 11.00 h)

question: The four lines of GSE167156 come from an 11-line survival and electrolyte-leakage screen. B73 and B104 are called chilling-tolerant and CML333 and M37W chilling-susceptible. B73 in GSE167881 is taken as tolerant on the same basis, although B73 survival under whole-plant chilling was 63% at 5 d, 7.4% at 6 d and 0% at 7 d.
proposed_answer: cold_tolerance: B73 tolerant, B104 tolerant, CML333 sensitive (paper: susceptible), M37W sensitive. genotype_class: B73 = B73; B104, CML333 and M37W = other inbred (background = the line itself).
evidence: Paper Results (OUP page); GSE167156 summary 'four maize lines with different chilling tolerance'

question: B73 leaf at 26 C vs whole-plant 4 C for 24 h occurs in both GSE167156 (2 vs 2 libraries) and GSE167881 (26S26R vs 4S4R, 3 vs 3). They were sequenced under separate submissions (BioProjects PRJNA703398 and PRJNA705456) and the paper's set-ups may differ (GSE167156 states pots 'in a 4 C chamber').
proposed_answer: Treat them as two independent experiments. Contrasts should be built within each series (other_factor is empty in GSE167156 and 'chilling site' in GSE167881); pooling decides whether both B73 leaf comparisons enter or only one.
evidence: runs.tsv bioprojects; GEO records of the two series

question: Seedlings were chilled at the three-leaf stage, 'about 10 days after germination', after a 1 d seed soak. No exact age or days after sowing is given.
proposed_answer: age_days = 10 (approximate, counted from germination); stage = three-leaf stage; stage_class = seedling.
evidence: Paper Methods (OUP page); GSE167881 sample characteristic 'Stage: three-leaf stage'

question: All 64 libraries are QuantSeq 3' mRNA-Seq FWD (Lexogen) sequenced single-end (79-86 nt) on a NextSeq500. They cannot be quantified like full-length RNA-seq (3' tag counting; UMI use not stated).
proposed_answer: Flag the study as 3' tag-seq when building the pipeline and contrasts; no change to the sample sheet.
evidence: GEO library construction field of GSM5098154 and GSM5114489; runs.tsv library_layout SINGLE and read_length 79-86

question: GEO says 'leaf' or 'leaf tissues'; the paper's sampling paragraph describes the basal two-thirds of the third leaf with major veins removed (written once for the whole study).
proposed_answer: Leaf tissue_detail uses the paper's description for both series.
evidence: Paper Methods sampling paragraph (OUP page)

question: The paper has no data statement in the retrieved text and describes Illumina NovaSeq PE150 (Biomarker/Bimaike); ENA lists BGISEQ-500 for PRJNA1111354. Is this the paper's dataset?
proposed_answer: Yes, accept. The BioSample isolates match the design exactly (Shen137 Control group, low temperature treatment, ABA, brassinolide, ABA+BR; 3 replicates each, 15 libraries, three-leaf stage), but the sequencing platform differs from the paper's text.
evidence: ENA PRJNA1111354: instrument BGISEQ-500, selection Oligo-dT, experiment titles 'RNA-Seq of maize: Control / low temperature treatment / Abscisic acid alleviates low temperature stress / Brassinolide alleviates ... / The interaction of ABA and br under low temperature stress'; collection_date 2023-11-26; PMC11989956 Methods.

question: Paper says 45 leaf samples (15 replicates x 3 plants) for RNA-seq in Results and '60 leaf samples' in the design section.
proposed_answer: 15 libraries (5 treatments x 3 reps, 3 plants pooled each) match the 15 runs; ignore the 60.
evidence: PMC11989956 Results 2.3 and Methods 4.2/4.4.1.

question: Treatment lasts 7 d at 10 C; no earlier time points. Hormones are applied every 2 d during the cold.
proposed_answer: time_h = 168 for all cold groups; CK has empty time_h (single-point control). Hormone factor recorded in other_factor/other_factor_level, with water as the 'none' level.
evidence: Paper Methods 4.2: 'cold treatment for 7 days', 'Every two days at 9:00 AM, 50 mL of the treatment solution was applied'.

question: LH82 (cold tolerant) was used for physiology only; only Shen137 was sequenced.
proposed_answer: No LH82 samples.
evidence: Paper Results 2.3: 'RNA-seq analysis was performed on leaf samples from the cold-sensitive inbred line Shen137'.

question: Paper says collar tissue of the second leaf; BioSample says 'blade'.
proposed_answer: Leaf (second leaf, collar region).
evidence: Paper Methods 4.4.1: 'Leaf collar tissues from the second leaf'; BioSample attribute tissue = blade.

question: Yu2021's full text was not readable (no PMC). Design details come from the abstract and Yu2023/Yu2024 methods on the same libraries. Are they the same experiment?
proposed_answer: Yes: B144 (tolerant) and Q319 (sensitive), 10-day-old seedlings at 25 C, 5 C for 0/12/24 h, 3 replicates, leaf, HiSeq 4000, 18 libraries. Curated here once; Yu2023 and Yu2024 borrow the runs.
evidence: Yu2021 abstract (PMID 33516847): 'growing both inbred lines at 5 C for 0, 12 and 24 h'; Yu2023 Methods (PMC10454290): seeds germinated 10 d in 25 C light incubator 12/12 h, then 5 C, leaf samples at 0, 12, 24 h, three replicates, 18 samples, NCBI deposit accessed 28 Sep 2020 (BioProject registered 28 Sep 2020 by Heilongjiang Academy of Agricultural Sciences).

item: 0 h control vs 25 C time-matched control
question: Is the untreated CK the 0 h sample or a time-matched 25 C control? Yu2024 (which uses 24 h vs control) says a group 'continued to grow at normal conditions'.
proposed_answer: Treat CK as the 0 h time-zero control (phase control, time_h 0). The deposited data hold only CK, 12 h and 24 h groups per line, so no separate 24 h 25 C control exists.
evidence: Yu2023 Methods: 'The treatment groups were named BCK, B12, B24 for B144 and QCK, Q12, Q24 for Q319 according to the treatment time (0, 12, 24 h)'; Yu2024 Methods: 12 samples (24 h vs control, 3 reps x 2 lines x 2) = the CK and 24 h subset of these libraries.

question: Photoperiod and light during the 5 C treatment are not stated; the 25 C regime is 12/12 h light/dark.
proposed_answer: Leave as noted in light_condition; flag as unknown.
evidence: Yu2023 Methods 2.1; Yu2021 full text not retrieved.

item: DEG counts differ between Yu2021 and Yu2023
question: Yu2023 reports DEGs only for 12 h and 24 h vs CK with logFC >= 2; not needed for curation.
proposed_answer: No action.
evidence: Yu2023 Results 3.1.

question: The four LH244 wild-type libraries here (SRR15096594-SRR15096597) have the same read counts and base counts as Zeng2024's WT runs (SRR27298835-SRR27298838), with the same cold/untreated and replicate pairing. They are the same libraries uploaded twice (MD5 differ).
proposed_answer: Count them once in pooling. Zeng2021's deposit is the earlier one (2021 vs 2023) and the data owner for the WT, so keep them here and mark the Zeng2024 WT runs as shared (also_used_by) or duplicates in runs.tsv; both sheets are complete so either can be chosen. The OE libraries are different (ZmRR1-OE here, ZmTIP4-OE there).
evidence: runs.tsv: read counts 36,823,370 / 33,652,561 / 38,073,710 / 30,332,664 in both studies; ENA run_alias WT_12_2, WT_12_1, WT_0_2, WT_0_1 vs WT-4-2, WT-4-1, WT-25-2, WT-25-1; Zeng2024 Methods 'RNA-seq ... conducted following established protocols (Zeng et al., 2021)'.

question: RNA-seq 'at 4 C for 0 h or 12 h'; the control is the 0 h sample taken at 25 C, not a time-matched warm control.
proposed_answer: time_h = 0 for controls, 12 for cold; contrasts will be 12 h cold vs 0 h (tag not_time_matched).
