evidence: Results 'Transcriptome analysis': 'incubated at 4 C for 0 h or 12 h'; Methods: 'with or without 12 h of 4 C treatment'; ENA titles 'untreated maize seedlings leaf'.

question: ZmRR1 overexpression enhances chilling tolerance in the paper; LH244 carries the susceptible HapB allele but is not itself labelled sensitive.
proposed_answer: ZmRR1-OE = tolerant; LH244 WT = NR.
evidence: Results 'ZmRR1 positively regulates maize chilling tolerance'; 'wild-type inbred line LH244 used in this study belongs to HapB'.

question: The ZmRR1-OE transgenic line ID is not given for the RNA-seq.
proposed_answer: Recorded as ZmRR1-OE (BioSample/ENA alias).
evidence: BioSample alias ZmRR1_OE; Methods mention >700 overexpression lines in LH244 without an ID.

item: WT libraries are the same as Zeng2021's
question: The four LH244 WT libraries (SRR27298835-SRR27298838) have the same read counts and base counts as Zeng2021's WT runs, with the same cold/untreated and replicate pairing; only the ZmTIP4-OE libraries are new.
proposed_answer: Count the WT libraries once in pooling: keep them as Zeng2021's (earlier deposit) and mark these four runs as shared or duplicates in runs.tsv. Both sheets are complete. The effective independent data of Zeng2024 are the four OE libraries.
evidence: runs.tsv read counts 36,823,370 / 33,652,561 / 38,073,710 / 30,332,664 in both studies; ENA run_alias WT-4-2, WT-4-1, WT-25-2, WT-25-1 vs Zeng2021 WT_12_2, WT_12_1, WT_0_2, WT_0_1; fastq MD5 differ.

item: age and replicates disagree with the shared WT
question: This paper says 14-day-old seedlings and (Methods) two biological replicates, but its Results say 'three independent experiments'; the WT libraries it deposits are Zeng2021's 10-day-old V2 samples.
proposed_answer: Sheet follows the Methods and the deposit: 2 replicates per group, age_days = 14 as stated (the WT libraries were 10 d in Zeng2021). The age mismatch for WT is noted, not corrected.
evidence: Methods 'RNA-seq': 'Two independent biological replicates were performed'; Results 'Transcriptome profiling': 'in three independent experiments'; Zeng2021 Methods '10-day-old maize seedlings (V2 stage)'.

item: TIP4;3-OE line ID and tolerance label
question: Line ID for the RNA-seq is not given; the paper shows TIP4;3 overexpression impairs cold tolerance.
proposed_answer: genotype ZmTIP4-OE (BioSample alias), class transgenic, background LH244, cold_tolerance sensitive (paper's label for the overexpression lines); WT NR.
evidence: Results 'Three TIP genes have a negative effect on the cold tolerance of maize'; BioSample alias ZmTIP4-OE.

question: Controls are called 'room temperature' in SRA and 'before ... exposure to 4 C' in the Methods.
proposed_answer: time_h = 0 for controls (the shared WT controls are 0 h samples in Zeng2021), time_h = 12 for cold.
evidence: Methods 'RT-qPCR and RNA-seq'; ENA titles 'room tempreature 14-day-old seedlings'.

question: Aliases bN-Maize-... (N = 1-3) are taken as the three independent biological replicates (planted and harvested on separate dates). Batch b2 was sequenced with 76 nt reads and about 17-29 M reads per library; b1 (51 nt, about 9-10 M reads) and b3 (51 nt, about 18-25 M reads) differ. Is b = replicate (and batch) as assumed?
proposed_answer: Yes, replicate = N in bN. Batch (b1, b2, b3) is confounded with replicate and, for b2, with read length/depth; contrasts should block on batch (replicate pairs are cold and control from the same batch).
evidence: Paper: 'three independent biological replicates ... planted and harvested on separate dates'; runs.tsv read_length and n_spots; BioSample aliases.

item: Tissue: whole plant or aboveground tissue
question: BioSample says tissue 'whole plant'; Methods say each sample is a pool of all aboveground tissue (leaf blades, ligules, leaf sheaths; no apical meristems, stems or roots) of 3-5 seedlings.

evidence: Methods of doi 10.1105/tpc.17.00354 (cold stress time course), BioSample attribute tissue.

question: Catalogue rows give genotype, temperatures and age as NR, and PMC full text via the PubMed tool is empty. Values read from the PMC web page: maize B73 (BioSample cultivar B73), 10 d after planting (BioSample dev_stage 10day; Methods: sorghum 12 d equals maize 10 d, planting dates staggered), control 29 °C day/23 °C night, cold 6 °C day and night, 12 h/12 h light cycle, cold onset immediately before the end of daylight.
proposed_answer: Recorded as read. The age of 10 d comes from the greenhouse experiment text and the BioSample; the Methods do not repeat it for the time course ('planted as above').
evidence: PMC5590507 Methods; BioSample attributes.

question: Samples were harvested from both control and cold treatments at 0.5, 1, 3, 6, 16 and 24 h after cold onset. Onset was at lights-off, so 0.5-6 h fall in the dark, 16 h is 4 h into the next light period and 24 h at the end of day. Alias suffix '05h' (and '05' in b2-Maize-cold-05) = 0.5 h.
proposed_answer: time_h = 0.5, 1, 3, 6, 16, 24 for both cold and control samples (time-matched); '05' read as 0.5 h. No time-zero samples.
evidence: Methods; aliases b1-Maize-cold-05h, b2-Maize-cold-05, b3-Maize-cold-05h.

item: Second BioProject PRJNA343268 not in runs.tsv
question: The paper cites two accessions: PRJNA344653 (this time course, 36 maize runs) and PRJNA343268 ('Cold stress and control on panicoid grass species', 30 runs over five species, maize aliases Maize-b1..b3-control and Maize-b1..b3-1d, i.e. 6 maize runs: the greenhouse experiment with 1 d cold vs control). It is listed as an uncatalogued maize cold record, not assigned to a study.
proposed_answer: Consider adding PRJNA343268 to Zhang2017 (greenhouse cold experiment, maize 3 replicates x control/1 d cold; harvested 3 h before lights on) in M1/M2; not curated here because its runs are not in runs.tsv.
evidence: ENA filereport for PRJNA343268 (checked 20 Oct 2026); uncatalogued_repository_records.tsv; Methods 'Accession Numbers'.

question: PRJNA344653 is also listed under Zeng2021 as role exclude (cited for comparison only).
proposed_answer: Zhang2017 owns the 36 maize runs; nothing to curate under Zeng2021.
evidence: accessions_resolved.tsv.

question: The 6 maize runs (3 control, 3 cold 24 h at 6 °C) were added to runs.tsv and this sheet. Controls stayed in the greenhouse (29/23 °C, 13 h day) while cold plants were moved to a 6 °C growth chamber (12 h day, much lower light), so the contrast mixes cold with the move and the light change.
proposed_answer: Keep as a separate contrast (other_factor = experiment); pool it with the time course only if Rubén agrees.
evidence: PMC5590507 Methods (greenhouse experiment paragraph)

question: Methods: seeds imbibed at 25 C for 6 h, then 'sampled at 2 h after imbibition on the germination paper' at 25 C (CK) or 10 C (LT). Is the cold exposure 2 h after a warm imbibition (acute cold) or low-temperature germination from imbibition (chronic)?
proposed_answer: Acute cold: phase = cold, time_h = 2, temperature 10 C vs 25 C control (the qRT-PCR validation at 2 h and 4 h of low temperature fits a 2 h cold exposure). If the authors meant germination at 10 C from imbibition the phase would be chronic and time_h empty.
evidence: Methods, 'Seed germination' and 'RNA-seq and analysis of DEGs'; qRT-PCR text 'under 2 h and 4 h of treatment with low temperatures'.

question: GEO titles use 55 and 102; the paper calls them Zao 8-3 (resistant, 55) and Ji 853 (sensitive, 102).
proposed_answer: Used the paper's line names and labels (tolerant / sensitive).
evidence: Results 'Differential gene expression': 'low-temperature-resistant maize line (Zao 8-3, referred to as 55) and the low-temperature-sensitive line (Ji 853, referred to as 102)'.

question: The raw-data accession is missing from the extracted paper text.
proposed_answer: GSE146666 (BioProject PRJNA611589) accepted by title and design match; sample titles carry the same line codes and conditions as the paper.
evidence: accessions_resolved.tsv; GEO titles CT_55e1 ... LT_102e3.

question: The paper calls Demeiya1 (flint) and Zhengdan958 (dent) 'varieties'/'cultivars' of northeast China and never says inbred or hybrid. Which genotype_class?
proposed_answer: NR for both. Zhengdan958 is widely known as a commercial hybrid (Zheng58 x Chang7-2) and Demeiya1 is probably one too, but the paper does not say; set to hybrid if you accept outside knowledge.
evidence: Methods 2.1 'Test Varieties and Experiment Design'; catalogue row Zhang2024 ('both northeast China cultivars').

question: The control is 15 C (the pre-germination temperature), which is itself a sub-optimal temperature for maize; cold is 5 C for 48 h after 72 h at 15 C.
proposed_answer: Kept as the paper defines it: control = 15 C (phase control), cold = 5 C (phase cold, time_h = 48). Contrast is cold shift vs cool control, so effect sizes may be smaller than 5 C vs 25 C.
evidence: Methods 2.1: 'germinated maize seeds continued to be incubated at 15 +- 0.5 C for 48 h in the dark' (CT) vs 5 +- 0.5 C (TS).

question: Dou2025 reuses these 12 runs (also_used_by).
proposed_answer: Curated once here; Dou2025 should borrow these samples, not add its own.
evidence: runs.tsv also_used_by = Dou2025; accessions_resolved note.

question: BioSample age is '48 h' (the treatment duration), while seeds had germinated 72 h at 15 C before treatment.
proposed_answer: age_days = 5 (72 h + 48 h from imbibition); stage text records the BioSample value.
evidence: Methods 2.1; BioSample age '48 h'.

item: 6 runs vs the paper's accession list
question: The Data Availability statement lists NCBI accession numbers (four per the extracted text; SRR13312968-72, five, per the PMC web page) but the project has six runs (SRR13312968-73), and the paper says 'six runs'.
proposed_answer: Keep all six (three 5 C, three 22 C; BioSample aliases M3d51-53 and M3dc1-3 cover exactly 3 + 3 and PCA in the paper shows three replicates). SRR13312973 (control replicate 1, M3dc1) is probably the one the statement omits.
evidence: accessions_resolved.tsv note; Results: 'A total of 55.14 GB clean data were produced by six runs ... three replicates of each sample'; ENA PRJNA686250 lists SRR13312968-SRR13312973.

question: ENA reports library_layout SINGLE with read lengths of 297-299 nt for HiSeq 2500 runs, which suggests merged or concatenated mates.
proposed_answer: Check one FASTQ (and read names) before M3 quantification; no change to the sheet.
evidence: runs.tsv: library_layout SINGLE, read_length 297-299, instrument Illumina HiSeq 2500.

question: Roots were sampled '3 days after cold treatment'; controls were kept at 22 C and sampled at the same time (not stated).
proposed_answer: time_h = 72 for cold; control is a single-point control (time_h empty).
evidence: Methods 'Plant Growth, Treatments, and Sampling'.

question: The paper removed these two 25 h cold samples of the replicated experiment (B73 and W22, replicate 2) for poor correlation with their biological replicates and substituted time-course samples TC64 and TC66. Both runs are in the repository. Keep them?
proposed_answer: Set include = FALSE for both (done in the sheet). B73 and W22 25 h cold then keep two replicates each (HY97+HY103; HY99+HY105). TC64 and TC66 stay as unreplicated time-course samples; do not add them as third replicates unless you decide to follow the authors.
evidence: Methods, RNA-seq data processing: "Two samples from the replicated experiment at the 25 h time point (HY91 and HY93) were also removed due to poor correlation with other biological replicates and substituted by two from the time-course samples (TC64 and TC66)".

question: The diversity panel should have 100 samples (25 inbreds x control/cold x 1/25 h) but KI11 has no NM_Cold_1h sample here (99 runs). Is that the sample dropped in library prep?
proposed_answer: Yes: the paper reports one sample omitted for too little cDNA. KI11 therefore has control 1 h, control 25 h and cold 25 h only, so no KI11 1 h cold contrast is possible.
evidence: Methods: "One sample did not meet the minimum cDNA content requirement during RNA-seq library preparation and was omitted"; 291 runs in PRJNA747925 vs 292 samples in the paper; NM11 absent from the run list.

question: What does the NM prefix mean? The paper does not define HY, TC or NM.
proposed_answer: HY = replicated hybrid experiment (Fig. 1 legend: "B73 samples from the hybrid experiment"), TC = time-course experiment, NM = diversity panel (25 inbreds x 4 = 100 samples matches the third experiment). Panel lines are used as named in the BioSample (KI3, KI11, Il14H, Mo18W, OH43, OH7B, ...). The paper makes no tolerance claims, so cold_tolerance = NR for all.
evidence: Methods: three experiments (replicated 126 samples, time course 66, panel 100); sample counts per prefix in runs.tsv match (HY 126, TC 66, NM 99).

question: B73, Mo17 and W22 occur in all three experiments (HY, TC, NM) at overlapping hours (e.g. B73 cold 1 h: 3 HY replicates, 1 TC, 1 NM), and replicate numbers repeat across experiments. How should groups be formed?
proposed_answer: other_factor = experiment with levels HY replicated inbred/F1 experiment, TC time-course experiment, NM 25-inbred diversity panel, so each cold sample pairs with controls of its own experiment (same genotype, same hour). Contrasts should be built within experiment; HY gives the replicated contrasts, TC and NM contrasts are unreplicated single-pair comparisons (decide at the contrast stage whether TC/NM B73, Mo17 and W22 pairs are pooled with HY).
evidence: Methods: three experiments run late May to early July 2019 with separate sample sets; alias prefixes HY, TC, NM in the BioSample treatment attribute.

item: Control for cold contrasts (time-matched vs time 0)
question: Each cold sample at 0.5-25 h has two possible comparators: the time-matched control and the 0 h control (HY and TC designs). Which should contrasts use?
proposed_answer: Use the time-matched control (same genotype, same hour) as the primary comparator, as the spec says, and keep the 0 h control as an optional secondary contrast. Both are in the sheet (phase control, time_h 0 or matched hour). The paper calls DEGs relative to both and keeps the intersection.
evidence: Results and Fig. 1D legend: DEGs "relative to the control sample collected at time 0 ... and relative to the control sample collected at the matching time point".

question: The paper says W22 lacks the 3 h and 8 h time points; the run list also lacks 1.5 h. Is a W22 1.5 h library missing?
proposed_answer: W22 has 11 cold/control libraries (control 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 25 h; cold 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 25 h) and none at 1.5, 3 and 8 h. The paper count of 66 time-course samples equals 3 genotypes x 25 libraries minus 9 (three W22 time points x control, cold, heat), so three W22 time points were never sequenced and the text (two points) undercounts. Authors imputed the missing points computationally; no imputed data are in the repository.
evidence: Methods: "due to low germination, several time points were omitted for W22"; "The two missing time points in W22 (3 and 8 h) were imputed from the two neighboring time points". TC runs per genotype: B73 8 cold + 9 control, Mo17 8 + 9, W22 5 + 6.

question: Methods name the hybrids B73xMo17, B73xW22 and Mo17xW22, but the Results introduction and the BioSample cultivar attribute give W22xB73 and W22xMo17. Reciprocal crosses or just naming?
proposed_answer: Keep the BioSample names (W22xB73, W22xMo17, B73xMo17); the paper uses the same names in the Results introduction. The female parent was not verified, so treat the order as a label only.
evidence: Results introduction: "B73xMo17, W22xB73, and W22xMo17"; Methods: "B73xMo17, B73xW22, and Mo17xW22"; BioSample cultivar attribute W22xB73, W22xMo17.

item: Plants per sample and plant age
question: Pool size is given as 3-4 seedlings (replicated and time-course experiments) and 3 seedlings (panel); the Methods closing sentence says 3 seedlings for each replicate. Plant age is "Day 9" without saying from when.
proposed_answer: pooled_plants left empty for HY and TC (3-4 per sample), 3 for NM. age_days = 9 for samples taken on Day 9 and 10 for the 25 h samples (treatment started on Day 9, 2 h after dawn); the day count is assumed to start at seed hydration (catalogue wording), not verified.
evidence: Methods: "each sample was a pool of tissue from 3 to 4 individual seedlings"; "hydrated for 24 h ... grown ... to the V2/V3 stage (Day 9)"; "V2 leaves from three maize seedlings were collected and pooled".

question: Cold is 6/2 °C day/night but temperature readings (Fig. 1B) are sensor traces, and the cold may take minutes to reach 6 °C. The 25 h cold samples passed through one night at 2 °C. Is time_h measured from the chamber switch?
proposed_answer: time_h is hours since stress onset (2 h after dawn on Day 9). temperature_C = 6 and temperature_night_C = 2 for all cold samples; controls 30/20. All sampling points fall in the light phase (2 h after dawn + 0 to 25 h).
evidence: Methods: "stress treatment (cold or heat) was initiated 2 h after dawn on Day 9 (i.e. time zero) ... The temperature settings for control, cold, and heat conditions were 30 °C/20 °C, 6 °C/2 °C, and 39 °C/29 °C".

question: The 0 h, 1 h and 25 h controls also serve as comparators for the heat treatment (heat runs excluded in runs.tsv). Any issue?
proposed_answer: No: controls are curated as plain control samples of this study; heat samples are not in the sheet.
evidence: runs.tsv exclude_reason "heat treatment, no cold contrast" for 57 runs.

question: runs.tsv says PAIRED but ENA lists a single FASTQ per run (SRRxxxx.fastq.gz, no _1/_2), and n_bases / n_spots = 2 x read length (150 for the 75 bp tissue libraries, 100 for the 50 bp LCM libraries). How are the mates stored?
proposed_answer: Probably both mates in one file (interleaved or concatenated). The M3 downloader and quantifier must check the layout of one file before processing; not resolved here.
evidence: runs.tsv: library_layout PAIRED, one fastq_urls entry, read_length 75 (80 tissue runs) and 50 (80 LCM runs), n_bases/n_spots exactly 150 or 100.

question: The regime is 16 h at 16 °C (day, T1) then 8 h at 12 °C (night, T2); control 26 then 18 °C. The BioSample temp attribute gives the temperature at sampling (T1 16/26, T2 12/18). Which goes in temperature_C?
proposed_answer: Following the spec (day value when day and night differ): temperature_C = 16 (cold) / 26 (control) and temperature_night_C = 12 / 18 for every sample, control_temperature_C = 26, so T1 and T2 differ only in time_h (16 vs 24 h cumulative cold). The temperature at sampling is in curation_note. If contrasts should use the sampling temperature instead, T2 would be 12 vs 18.
evidence: Results and Fig. 1A legend: "time point T1 refers to growth for 16 h at 16 °C, and T2 for an add-on period of 8 h at 12 °C"; Methods: control 26/18 °C, 16 h light/8 h dark.

question: For LCM libraries the number in the title (CD1-CD5, CT1-CT8) is not the replicate (e.g. T1-CD2-en is replicate 2, T1-CD2-ep replicate 1). Which to use?
proposed_answer: The BioSample "biological replicate" attribute (rep1-rep4), which gives exactly four replicates per tissue/cell type, condition and time point (verified for all 40 groups). Title numbers look like a plate or sample-set index.
evidence: Run list: every group of tissue x condition x time point has replicates 1-4 once; title numbers repeat across cell types.

question: The titles use PR, MZ, EZ, CO, St (bulk, underscore titles) and co, en, ep, pp, xp (LCM, hyphen titles). The mapping to the paper's sample types was inferred. Correct?
proposed_answer: Bulk: PR = whole primary root (organ level), MZ = meristematic zone (apical 2 mm), EZ = elongation zone, CO = Co_T (epidermis + cortical parenchyma + endodermis of the differentiation zone), St = stele, matching the BioSample tissue text (primary root, meristematic zone, elongation zone, cortex, stele). LCM: ep epidermis, co cortex, en endodermis, pp phloem-pole pericycle, xp xylem-pole pericycle (BioSample tissue). CD = cold and CT = control (BioSample treatment). Table S6 (listed in the paper as primers) was not needed. Do not pool Co_T with LCM cortex: Co_T contains epidermis and endodermis.
evidence: Methods and Fig. 1 legend on the OUP page; BioSample tissue and treatment attributes for all 160 runs.

item: Root hairs and mutants not sequenced
question: The catalogue lists root hairs and the rth5, rth6, dreb2.1 and DREB2.1-overexpression lines, but the BioProject has only PE0075 libraries. Are there other transcriptome datasets?
proposed_answer: No root-hair or mutant RNA-seq is in PRJNA852372 (160 PE0075 runs: 5 tissues + 5 cell types x 4 replicates x 2 conditions x 2 time points). Root hairs and mutants/B73 were analysed by RT-qPCR and phenotyping only, so no rows for them.
evidence: OUP page: "Root hairs of primary roots were used for expression analyses" (Fig. 4, RT-qPCR); RNA-seq described for whole primary roots, four tissues and five cell types, PE0075 only.

item: Time of harvest and cold onset
question: The paper does not give clock times. Was cold applied at the start of the light period, and were T2 samples harvested in the dark?
proposed_answer: time_h = 16 (T1) and 24 (T2) from cold onset, assumed at the start of treatment (4 d after germination). T1 follows the 16 h day phase and T2 the following 8 h night phase, so T2 was harvested at the end of the dark period; recorded in light_condition. Controls were harvested at the same times (time-matched).
evidence: Methods: "The first sampling (time point 1) was carried out after 16 h of growth at 26 °C (control) or 16 °C (cold)" and "The second sampling (time point 2) was carried out after another 8 h of growth".

question: BioSample age is 5 days for all samples, but the paper says treatment started 4 d after germination (so T1 ~4.7 d and T2 ~5 d after germination).
proposed_answer: age_days = 5 for all (BioSample value, first source in the spec); the paper value is in the stage text.
evidence: Methods: "Four days after germination in paper rolls under control conditions ... seedlings were subsequently subjected to control or cold treatment"; BioSample attribute age "5 days".

item: Pooling for LCM samples and quality
question: The number of cells or seedlings per LCM sample is not reported, and RNA quality of LCM libraries is lower (RIN 5.5-7.2 vs >= 8 for bulk tissues). Include all?
proposed_answer: Include all 80 LCM libraries (pooled_plants left empty); the 50 bp reads and low-input RNA may give noisier libraries, to be judged by library QC in M3/M4, not here.
evidence: Methods: cell-type RNA with PicoPure kit, RIN 5.5-7.2, 2.9-18.8 ng/µl; bulk RNA RIN >= 8.

question: The LCM sections were taken 1.75-2.25 mm from the root tip, but Mz is defined as the apical 2 mm. Should LCM cell types be treated as part of the meristematic/transition zone?
proposed_answer: tissue_detail says "meristematic-zone cross sections 1.75-2.25 mm from root tip" as in the Fig. 1 legend ("5 root cell types of the meristematic zone"). Contrasts should only compare each cell type with its own control, not with bulk zones.
evidence: Fig. 1 legend and Methods: sections cut "1.75 to 2.25 mm from the root tip".
